articles.title: The Box of Copper That Made the Handle Harder to Press
articles.summaryZh: 同牌号、同尺寸的铜卡扣，换一盒就突然难压。秦岚翻开加工记录，发现两盒在到达这道工序之前，走过了不同的路。
articles.summary: A new box of copper clips suddenly makes the press harder to operate, although the grade and dimensions match. Qin Lan checks what happened to each box before it reached this step.
storyParagraphsZh: 秦岚正在给一组桌灯装最后的铜卡扣。前面几十片都顺利压出圆角，换到下一盒时，手柄却明显更沉，卡扣还没到她要的形状。盒子上写着同一个铜牌号，零件的宽度、厚度和进入这道工序前的弯形也相同。她没有继续硬压，因为再加力之前，得先弄清这一盒为什么变得不一样。
她把两盒的加工经历重新对上。较难弯的那盒为了修正前一道外形，曾在室温下反复弯折、整形；另一盒来自同批铜材，在主要成形之后做过退火，也就是按既定工艺进行的受控加热处理，之后只裁切到需要的尺寸，没有再做明显的冷态塑性整形。平时大家只看铜牌号就能拿料，是因为加工经历大致一致；这一次，材料名称相同，状态却不再相同。
秦岚找出两条尺寸和起始弯形相同的余片，一条来自反复冷态整形的那盒，一条来自退火后仅裁切的那盒。她把两条依次放进同一只带测力表的压具，让压头走到同一个既定位置。到达那里时，反复冷态整形过的余片需要更大的力；卸载后，两条都留下了新的弯曲。
秦岚把退火后未再明显冷作的那盒搬到这道弯曲工位，另一盒先撤回待用盘，等下一批只需轻微修整的用途再核对。原来两盒可以顺手交替拿，现在得重新分拣，装配同事每次取料也要多确认一步。她保住了这一批继续成形的安排，却失去了混拿库存的便利。
做到这一排灯的最后一个卡扣时，秦岚先松开压具手柄，取下刚弯好的铜件，再把它按进灯罩边缘。卡扣发出一声清脆的“咔”。她把装好的灯推到同事手边，待用盘里那盒反复整形过的铜件则留在另一张工作台上。
storyParagraphs: Qin Lan is fitting the final copper clips to a set of table lamps. The first several dozen form smoothly into their rounded shape, but when she switches to the next box, the handle becomes noticeably harder to press and the clips still have not reached the shape she needs. The box carries the same copper grade, and the parts have the same width, thickness, and starting bend before this step. She does not keep forcing the handle down. Before applying more force, she needs to know why this box is behaving differently.

She retraces the processing history of the two boxes. The harder-to-bend parts had been bent back and reshaped several times at room temperature to correct an earlier shape. The other box came from the same copper batch, but after its main forming step it underwent annealing—a controlled heating treatment—and was then only cut to size, without further substantial cold plastic forming. The team usually picks parts by grade because their processing histories are similar. This time, the name is the same, but the state is different.

Qin Lan finds two offcuts with the same dimensions and starting bend, one from the repeatedly cold-formed box and one from the annealed-then-cut box. She places them in turn in the same small press with a force gauge and moves the press head to the same specified position. At that position, the repeatedly cold-formed piece requires more force. After unloading, both pieces retain a new bend.

Qin Lan moves the box that was annealed without substantial later cold working to the bending station. The other box goes back to a holding tray, to be checked for a later use requiring only light adjustment. The team had routinely taken parts from either box; now the boxes have to be sorted, and the assembly workers must check one more detail when taking a part. She keeps this batch’s forming work moving, at the cost of the old convenience.

For the last clip in this row of lamps, Qin Lan first releases the press handle, removes the newly bent part, and then presses it into the edge of the lampshade. It snaps into place with a crisp click. She slides the completed lamp toward her colleague. The box of repeatedly reshaped copper parts remains in its holding tray on another workbench.
articles.overallZh: 铜的成分相同，加工历史却可能不同。冷态塑性加工会改变内部结构，通常使后续永久成形更费力；适当退火可让铜更容易继续成形。因此，判断材料的加工表现，还要看它目前处在哪种状态。
articles.overall: Copper parts with the same composition can have different processing histories. Cold plastic working changes their internal structure and generally raises resistance to further permanent forming; appropriate annealing can make forming easier again. Understanding their processing behavior therefore also requires knowing their current state.
explanationParagraphsZh: 位错是金属晶体中的线状缺陷，它们的运动参与塑性变形，也就是留下永久形状的变化。铜经过冷态塑性加工后，位错数量和相互阻碍会增加，继续变形通常需要更高应力。适当退火可通过回复、再结晶等内部结构变化，使铜重新更容易塑性成形，化学成分却不必改变。
最小核对：两条同成分、同尺寸、同起始弯形的铜试样，在同一压具中达到同一位置时，可以需要不同的力。这里比较的是各自加工状态下的继续成形表现，不能据此推断弹性模量也变了。
explanationParagraphs: Dislocations are line defects in a metal crystal. Their motion contributes to plastic deformation—a change that leaves a permanent shape. Cold plastic working of copper increases dislocations and their interference with one another, so further deformation generally requires higher stress. Appropriate annealing can make copper easier to form again through internal changes such as recovery and recrystallization, without changing its chemical composition.

Minimal check: two copper specimens with the same composition, dimensions, and starting bend can require different forces to reach the same position in the same press. This compares their resistance to further forming in their respective processing states; it does not establish that elastic modulus has changed.

moduleZh.intro: 把材料牌号和加工状态分开看：先确认几何可比，再观察不同加工经历如何改变继续塑性成形的难易。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 铜牌号相同，为什么继续弯曲时所需力仍可能不同
diagramSteps: 进入最后工序时，两组同批铜件的尺寸和起始弯形相同
一组此前反复经历冷态塑性整形，另一组主要成形后退火且随后只裁切
将可比余片放入同一带测力表的压具，并让压头达到同一既定位移
反复冷态整形的余片在该位移下需要更大的力
据此把后续明显塑性成形任务优先分配给更适合继续成形的加工状态
diagramStepNotes: 比较前要控制尺寸和起始几何，否则弯曲阻力也会因几何不同而变化。
退火之后若再次进行大量冷态塑性整形，材料状态仍可能再次改变，因此故事明确后续只有裁切。
同一位移下比较所需力，不等于两条试样承受同一载荷。
这里关注继续塑性变形抗力，不把它等同于弹性模量。
虚构余片对照只帮助理解机制，不证明所有铜材或所有工艺都会表现成同一数值差异。
mapping: 同一个铜牌号 → 化学成分信息相近，但不能独自说明当前加工状态。
反复冷态整形 → 改变内部位错结构并提高继续塑性变形的阻力。
退火后仅裁切 → 保留一个较适合继续塑性成形的状态入口。
同位移下更高测力读数 → 当前继续变形阻力不同的教学观察。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只讨论同成分铜在不同加工状态下继续发生塑性变形的差异。弯曲力还受厚度、宽度、初始曲率、支承和加载方式影响，因此比较必须保持几何和条件可比。加工硬化或更高屈服抗力不等于弹性模量必然提高；退火也不意味着消除所有内部缺陷。本文不提供通用退火参数、材料安全等级或完整选材依据。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果一盒铜件标着“已退火”，后来又反复冷态整形，下一次拿来成形还能只凭这个旧标签判断吗？为什么？

module.intro: Separate material grade from processing state: first make the geometry comparable, then observe how different processing histories can change the difficulty of further plastic forming.
module.diagramTitle: If the Copper Grade Is the Same, Why Can the Force Needed for Further Bending Still Differ?
diagramSteps: At entry to the final step, the two groups from the same copper batch have matching dimensions and starting bends
One group has undergone repeated cold plastic forming, while the other was annealed after main forming and then only cut
Place comparable offcuts in the same force-instrumented press and move the press head to the same specified displacement
The repeatedly cold-formed offcut requires more force at that displacement
Assign further substantial plastic forming preferentially to the processing state better suited to continued forming
diagramStepNotes: Dimensions and starting geometry must be comparable, because bending resistance can also change with geometry.
If substantial cold plastic forming occurs again after annealing, the material state can change again, so the story specifies that only cutting follows annealing.
The comparison is force required at the same displacement, not two specimens carrying the same load.
The focus is resistance to further plastic deformation, not elastic modulus.
The fictional offcut comparison helps explain the mechanism but does not prove that all copper or all processing routes will show the same numerical difference.
mapping: The same copper grade → similar composition information, but not enough to specify the current processing state.
Repeated cold forming → a change in dislocation structure that raises resistance to further plastic deformation.
Annealed and then only cut → a processing state that remains more suitable for further plastic forming in this teaching example.
Higher force at the same displacement → a teaching observation of different resistance to continued deformation.
module.boundary: This article only discusses differences in further plastic deformation of copper with the same composition but different processing states. Bending force is also affected by thickness, width, initial curvature, support, and loading method, so geometry and test conditions must be comparable. Work hardening or higher yield resistance does not mean elastic modulus must increase; annealing also does not mean every internal defect has been removed. This article provides no universal annealing parameters, material safety rating, or complete basis for material selection.
module.reflection: If a box of copper parts is labelled “annealed” but is then repeatedly cold-formed, is the old label enough to judge how it will form next? Why or why not?

referencesZh.citation: Stoebe, T. Work Hardening and Annealing of Copper. MatEd materials-education module, University of Washington; copyright Edmonds Community College 2007.
referencesZh.use: 支持铜在塑性加工过程中因位错结构变化而提高继续变形阻力，以及退火可使材料恢复到更易继续塑性变形的状态；不用于提供通用热处理配方、声称清除全部缺陷或推断弹性模量必然增加。

references.citation: Stoebe, T. Work Hardening and Annealing of Copper. MatEd materials-education module, University of Washington; copyright Edmonds Community College 2007.
references.use: Supports the increase in resistance to further deformation caused by changes in dislocation structure during plastic working of copper, and the ability of annealing to return copper to a state that is easier to plastically deform. It is not used to provide a universal heat-treatment recipe, claim that every defect is removed, or infer that elastic modulus necessarily increases.

articles.title: One Board, Two Directions
articles.summaryZh: 何玥想让三本推荐书摆在一个轻薄的小架子上，细横条却弯得太明显。她不愿先把架子加厚，目光转向了余料上的木纹。
articles.summary: He Yue wants a slim display shelf for three recommended books, but its narrow rail bends too much. Before making the shelf thicker, she takes another look at the grain in the remaining board.
storyParagraphsZh: 书店想在收银台旁摆一个轻薄的小书架，只放三本当月推荐的精装书。何玥做出的第一版外形很好看，可书一放上去，中间那根细木条就弯得比她预想的明显。她不想简单把横条做厚，因为那会把整套架子的轻巧感一起丢掉。
拆下横条后，她才认真看清切料方向：这块直纹实木板上切出的旧条，主要木纹沿着短边的方向横过条宽。余料还有足够位置，她从相邻区域重新切出一根同样长、宽、厚的样条，这一次让主要木纹沿着木条的长边走。她改变的是从板上取料的方向，不是把旧木条翻个面。
何玥把两根样条分别跨在相同间距的支点上，在中间放同一个小砝码。横纹样条下弯得更明显，纹路沿条长的样条只微微下沉。她把砝码拿下，又交换测试顺序重复了一次，差别仍看得出来。她把沿条长取纹的那根放到样架旁，决定先拿这个方向试下一版。
她照这个取向重做了中间横条，把完整书架放回收银台，重新摆上原来的三本精装书继续观察。为了让关键横条顺着这个方向取料，木板的切料布局没有以前自由，边角余料多了一些。
第二天下午，何玥从书架最下面抽出一本，又把它塞回去。新的中间横条没有像第一版那样明显下垂。旧横条没有被扔掉，她把它截短，装到了书架背面一个只起装饰作用的小位置；工作台上则留下了几块因为取向受限而不好再利用的木料边角。
storyParagraphs: The bookstore wants a slim, lightweight display shelf beside the checkout counter for just three hardcover books from the month's recommendations. He Yue's first version looks good, but once the books are placed on it, the narrow center rail bends more than she expected. She does not want to solve the problem simply by making the rail thicker, because that would also take away the light appearance of the whole shelf.

After removing the rail, she looks carefully at its cutting direction. In the old strip cut from this straight-grained solid board, the main grain runs in the short-edge direction, across the strip’s width. There is enough material left for another specimen of the same length, width, and thickness from a neighboring area, this time with the grain along the long edge. She changes the direction in which she cuts from the board, rather than turning the old strip over.

He Yue places the two specimens on supports with the same spacing and puts the same small weight at the center. The cross-grain specimen bends more, while the one with grain along its length deflects only slightly. She removes the weight and repeats the comparison in the opposite order. The difference remains visible. She sets the along-grain specimen beside the prototype shelf and chooses that cutting direction for the next version.

She remakes the center rail in that orientation, returns the complete shelf to the checkout counter, and puts the same three hardcover books back on it to continue observing. Cutting the critical rail in that direction makes the layout on the board less flexible and leaves more offcuts.

The next afternoon, He Yue pulls the bottom book from the shelf and slides it back in. The new center rail does not sag as noticeably as the first version. She does not throw away the old, more flexible rail. Instead, she shortens it and uses it as a small decorative strip on the back of the shelf, where it does not perform the same bending task. Several awkwardly shaped offcuts remain on the workbench because the cutting direction is now constrained.
articles.overallZh: 各向异性指材料性质会随方向变化。木材内部的纤维和组织有方向性，因此比较同一种木材的变形表现，除了尺寸和受力条件，还要问它是沿哪个方向取出的。
articles.overall: Anisotropy means that a material’s properties depend on direction. Wood’s fibres and internal structure are directional, so comparing deformation in the same kind of wood requires knowing the specimen’s orientation as well as its dimensions and loading conditions.
explanationParagraphsZh: 木材不是各个方向都表现相同的材料。其内部纤维和组织具有方向性，所以沿纤维方向与横向于纤维的弹性响应可以不同；工程上还会进一步区分纵向、径向和弦向。
最小核对：从同板相邻区域取两根等长、等宽、等厚的样条，在相同支承间距和同一个小载荷下，比较它们的下弯距离，也就是挠度。不同取向可以有不同结果；天然差异仍然存在，一对样条不能给出所有木材的固定性能比。
explanationParagraphs: Wood does not behave identically in every direction. Its fibres and internal structure are directional, so elastic response along the fibre direction can differ from response across the fibres. Engineering descriptions further distinguish longitudinal, radial, and tangential directions.

Minimal check: take two specimens of equal length, width, and thickness from neighboring parts of the same board. With the same support span and small load, compare how far they bend—their deflection. Different orientations can give different results, but natural variation remains, and one pair cannot establish a fixed property ratio for all wood.

moduleZh.intro: 先让样条尺寸、支承和小载荷可比，再把取向作为需要检查的一个条件，观察它如何影响变形判断。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 同一块木板，为什么换一个取样方向就可能弯得不同
diagramSteps: 第一版横条的主要木纹横过条宽，放上三本书后下弯明显
从同一块板相邻区域重新切出相同长、宽、厚的样条，让主要木纹沿条长
将两根样条放在相同支承间距上并施加同一个小载荷
纹路沿条长的样条在这次教学比较中下弯更少
下一版书架改用该取向的横条，再回到完整三本书展示任务中继续检查
diagramStepNotes: 旧横条的木纹沿短边方向，横过条宽。
新样条的木纹沿条长；这是重新取样，不是翻面。
尺寸、支承间距和载荷保持可比；不能拿长短厚薄不同的条直接判取向。
本次结果还可能受局部含水率、密度和天然特征影响，不能给出通用刚度比例。
再看完整书架在原任务中的表现，仍不把小样观察当成真实结构设计值。
mapping: 第一版横纹横条 → 一个在该使用方向下弯曲较明显的取向。
纹路沿条长的新样条 → 改变材料方向后的可比试片。
相同支点与小砝码 → 为了缩小几何和加载替代解释的教学条件。
增加的边角余料 → 为指定取料方向付出的材料利用率代价。
moduleZh.boundary: 木材的机械性能受纵向、径向、弦向方向以及含水率、密度和天然缺陷等多种因素影响。本篇只用两根相邻样条说明“方向可能改变变形表现”，不提供真实结构设计值，也不建立所有方向的普遍优劣排序。不同几何、支承或载荷条件下的弯曲不能直接归因于各向异性。
moduleZh.reflection: 有人拿一根较短木条和一根较长木条比较下弯，即使两者是同种木材，能只把差异归因于取向吗？还应先让哪些条件可比？

module.intro: Make specimen dimensions, support, and the small load comparable, then examine orientation as one condition that matters when interpreting deformation.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can a Different Cutting Direction Change Bending Even Within the Same Board?
diagramSteps: The first center rail has its main grain running across the strip width and bends noticeably under the three books
Cut another specimen from a neighboring area of the same board with the same length, width, and thickness, but with the main grain running along the strip length
Place both specimens on supports with the same spacing and apply the same small load
In this teaching comparison, the specimen with grain along the strip length bends less
Use that orientation for the next center rail and then return to the complete three-book display task
diagramStepNotes: The old rail’s grain runs in the short-edge direction, across its width.
The new specimen’s grain runs along its length. This requires a new cut, not merely flipping the old strip.
Keep dimensions, support span, and load comparable; strips of different lengths or thicknesses do not isolate orientation.
Local moisture, density, and natural features can also affect the result, which does not give a universal stiffness ratio.
Return to the complete shelf’s original task without treating a small-specimen observation as a structural design value.
mapping: First center rail with grain across the width → an orientation that bends more noticeably in this use direction.
New specimen with grain along the strip length → a comparable specimen with a different material orientation.
Same supports and small weight → teaching conditions used to reduce geometric and loading alternatives.
Extra awkward offcuts → the material-utilization cost of specifying cutting direction.
module.boundary: Wood mechanical properties are influenced by longitudinal, radial, and tangential direction as well as moisture content, density, and natural features. This article uses only two neighboring specimens to show that direction can change deformation behavior; it does not provide structural design values or establish a universal ranking of all directions. Bending tests with different geometry, support, or loading conditions cannot be attributed directly to anisotropy.
module.reflection: Someone compares bending in a short strip and a longer strip of the same wood species. Can the difference be attributed to orientation alone? Which conditions should first be made comparable?

referencesZh.citation: Senalik, C. A., & Farber, B. (2021). Chapter 5: Mechanical properties of wood. In Wood handbook—wood as an engineering material. General Technical Report FPL-GTR-282. U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Forest Products Laboratory.
referencesZh.use: 支持木材具有纵向、径向和弦向等材料方向，弹性性质随方向而异，并会受到含水率、密度和天然特征影响；不用于把一对教学样条的结果外推为真实结构设计值或所有木材的固定比例。

references.citation: Senalik, C. A., & Farber, B. (2021). Chapter 5: Mechanical properties of wood. In Wood handbook—wood as an engineering material. General Technical Report FPL-GTR-282. U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Forest Products Laboratory.
references.use: Supports the existence of longitudinal, radial, and tangential material directions in wood, differences in elastic properties by direction, and the influence of moisture content, density, and natural features. It is not used to extrapolate one teaching pair of specimens into structural design values or fixed ratios for all wood.

articles.summaryZh: 纪岑要为三个社区安排展览。三个场地规格相同，却各有一副新框架的采购计划；她试着让同一副框架走到下一场。
storyParagraphsZh: 城市阅读计划要在三个社区连续办三场同规格的小型展览。纪岑拿到的第一份执行方案很直接：第一场做一副新框架和一套信息板，第二场再做一副，第三场再做一副，三场合计三副框架、三套内容不同的信息板。板材上还标着可回收，她最开始并没有觉得这个安排有什么明显问题。
直到她把三个场地的尺寸图叠在一起，才发现展位规格相同，真正每场变化的主要是文字和图片。她把方案改成一副可拆装框架配三套信息板，但很快发现图纸画得出来，并不代表第二场真的会再用上。第一场结束以后谁拆、谁运回去、仓库放哪里、谁在第二场前检查，都得先安排好。
第一场结束当晚，工作人员把框架拆进周转箱，没有送去废料处理。第二天，它被运回仓库清洁和检查，随后带着新信息板进入下一个社区。第二场展览结束时，纪岑摸了摸框架边缘留下的一处小擦痕。这还是第一场那一副框架，已经完成了一次实际再用。
第二场结束后，框架再次被收回。检查时发现一只脚垫磨损，团队更换了这个小部件，重新清洁框架，再送去第三个社区。返运、仓储、清洁、检查和脚垫更换都增加了实际工作和费用；三套信息板也仍然各自制作。第三场使用的不是一副凭空“零成本”的框架，而是经过维护后继续保留下来的同一副。
第三场开门前，工作人员把最后一套信息板装上已经有使用痕迹的框架。纪岑确认脚垫和连接状态后站到一旁。等这场活动也结束，团队才把三场账合到一起：实际制作一副框架，而非原计划的三副；首次使用后，又实际再用了两次。三套信息板、换掉的脚垫和运输清洁等投入仍各有去向和账目。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用三场同规格展览说明循环设计的一个入口：在方案开始时，不仅考虑材料报废后是否理论可回收，还要把产品如何维护、收回、运输、检查并实际再次使用一起设计进去。产品真正保持使用和价值，比单独贴上“可回收”标签更能说明循环路径是否发生。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例只比较框架这一部分。原方案三场分别制作三副新框架；修改后只制作一副框架，并在第一场后收回用于第二场、第二场后再次收回用于第三场，因此框架制作数量由3副变为1副，并发生两次实际再使用。三套不同内容的信息板仍分别制作，不计入这个“框架3→1”的数量比较。
实际再用还依赖拆装、返运、仓储、清洁、检查、配件和再次安装等配套条件。如果这些环节不可行，理论上可拆或可回收也不保证产品真的继续使用。框架数量下降本身也不能证明总重量、总费用、碳排放或其他环境影响一定下降；若要回答这些问题，还需要相应的数据和进一步比较。

moduleZh.intro: 先固定三场相同规格的使用任务，再检查一副框架能否通过真实的收回、维护和再安装路径跨场继续使用。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么一副可拆框架只有真正回来并再次使用，才算形成了再用路径
diagramSteps: 原方案为三场活动分别制作三副新框架，并分别配置三套信息板
修改方案只制作一副可拆装框架，但三套不同内容的信息板仍分别制作
第一场结束后实际拆卸、返运、清洁和检查同一副框架，并用于第二场
第二场结束后再次收回框架，更换磨损脚垫并维护后用于第三场
最终记录三场共使用一副框架、发生两次实际再使用，同时把信息板、配件和物流维护另行记录
diagramStepNotes: 三场规格相同是本例能够共用同一副框架的重要条件；场地或功能不同可能改变结果。
框架数量3→1只描述框架制作数量，不包括三套信息板。
第一次实际再用需要真实发生的返运、检查和再次安装，而不是图纸上写着‘可重复使用’。
脚垫更换说明维护和可获得配件可能是继续使用路径的一部分。
运输、清洁、仓储、人工和其他材料投入仍需另记，不能从框架数量下降直接推出总体环境或经济优势。
mapping: 原方案三副新框架 → 每场活动重新制作完整框架的线性方案。
一副跨三场框架 → 通过两次实际收回和再使用保持产品价值。
磨损脚垫的更换 → 维护和配件支持使产品继续使用的一个具体环节。
三套信息板 → 随内容变化仍需单独制作、不属于框架3→1数量节省的部分。
返运、清洁和仓储 → 让理论可再用变成实际再用所需的运营系统。
moduleZh.boundary: 循环设计并不等于任何情况下都优先重复使用或回收，也不保证可拆产品一定耐用、安全、经济或真正被收回。本例只证明在三场相同规格任务中，同一副框架被实际使用三次、发生两次再使用。信息板、小部件、运输、清洁、仓储和人工仍有额外投入；没有进一步生命周期或成本分析时，不能声称方案必然碳排更低、总成本更低、无污染或实现100%回收。循环经济还包括减少废物和污染、循环产品与材料以及再生自然等更广原则，本篇只取“保持产品继续使用”这一入口。
moduleZh.reflection: 假如同一副框架已经用过两场，第三个场地却换了尺寸。能凭“已经再用过”就确定它适用第三场、总体环境影响也更低吗？还缺哪些信息？

referencesZh.citation: Ellen MacArthur Foundation. (2024, August 21). Circular economy principles.
referencesZh.use: 支持循环经济由设计驱动，包括消除废物和污染、循环产品与材料以及再生自然，并讨论维护、重复使用和翻新等保持产品价值的路径；本篇只聚焦实际再使用这一入口，不据此声称虚构展架已实现更低总影响或成本。

referencesZh.citation: European Commission. (2020). Investing in the Circular Economy: A Blueprint for a Green Recovery. Publications Office of the European Union.
referencesZh.use: 支持通过更耐用、可维修的设计以及回收物流来维持产品和材料价值，并支持重复使用和翻新等路径需要配套系统；该政策资料不作为本虚构展架的成本、材料、能耗或环境表现实证。

articles.title: The Frame’s Next Stop
articles.summary: Ji Cen is planning exhibitions in three communities. The spaces match, yet each event is set to buy a new frame. She tries to give the same frame a place at the next event.
storyParagraphs: The city reading programme is preparing three small exhibitions in three communities, all with the same spatial requirements. Ji Cen's first implementation plan is straightforward: make one new frame and one information-panel set for the first event, another frame for the second, and another for the third. Across the three events, that means three frames and three information-panel sets with different content. The board material is also labelled recyclable, so at first she sees no obvious problem with the arrangement.

Only after she overlays the dimension drawings for the three venues does she notice that the exhibition spaces are the same size and that what mainly changes from event to event is the text and imagery. She changes the plan to one demountable frame with three information-panel sets, but quickly realizes that being able to draw a reusable frame does not mean the second event will actually use it. Who dismantles it after the first event, who transports it back, where the warehouse stores it, and who inspects it before the second event all have to be arranged in advance.

On the evening after the first event, staff dismantle the frame into a transit case instead of sending it for waste handling. The next day it returns to the warehouse for cleaning and inspection, then goes with new information panels to the next community. After the second exhibition ends, Ji Cen runs her hand over a scuff on the frame edge. It is the same frame from the first event, now with one completed reuse.

After the second event, the frame is recovered again. During inspection, the team finds that one foot pad is worn, replaces that small part, cleans the frame again, and sends it to the third community. Return transport, storage, cleaning, inspection, and replacement of the foot pad all add real work and cost; the three sets of information panels are also still produced separately. The third event is not using a magically 'zero-cost' frame, but the same frame retained in service through maintenance.

Before the third event opens, staff fit the final panel set to the visibly used frame. Ji Cen checks the foot pad and connections, then steps aside. Only after this event also ends does the team total the three-event record: one frame was actually made, rather than the three originally planned, and it was reused twice after its first use. The three panel sets, replaced foot pad, transport and cleaning still have their own material flows and costs.
articles.overall: This article uses three same-specification exhibitions to introduce one aspect of design for circularity: at the beginning of a design, it is not enough to consider whether material might theoretically be recyclable at end of life. The product and its supporting system also need to be designed for maintenance, return, transport, inspection, and actual reuse. Keeping a product in use and retaining its value in practice is more concrete evidence of a circular pathway than a recyclability label alone.
explanationParagraphs: This example compares only the frame portion of the task. Under the original plan, three new frames would be made separately for the three events. Under the revised plan, only one frame is made, then recovered after the first event and used for the second, and recovered again after the second event and used for the third. Frame production therefore changes from 3 frames to 1, with two actual reuse events. The three information-panel sets with different content are still made separately and are not included in the frame-count comparison.

Actual reuse also depends on supporting conditions such as dismantling, return transport, storage, cleaning, inspection, spare parts, and reinstallation. If those steps are not workable, being theoretically demountable or recyclable does not guarantee continued use. A lower frame count also does not by itself prove lower total mass, total cost, carbon emissions, or other environmental impacts. Those questions require additional data and separate comparison.

module.intro: Hold the three same-specification events constant, then check whether one frame can actually continue in use across events through a real return, maintenance, and reinstallation pathway.
module.diagramTitle: Why Does a Demountable Frame Count as Reuse Only After It Actually Comes Back and Is Used Again?
diagramSteps: The original plan makes three new frames for three events and separately provides three information-panel sets
The revised plan makes only one demountable frame, while the three different information-panel sets are still made separately
After the first event, actually dismantle, return, clean, and inspect the same frame and use it at the second event
After the second event, recover the frame again, replace the worn foot pad, maintain it, and use it at the third event
Finally record one frame used across all three events and two actual reuse events, while accounting separately for information panels, parts, transport, and maintenance
diagramStepNotes: The same event specifications are an important condition for sharing the frame in this example; different venues or functions could change the result.
The frame-count change from 3 to 1 describes only the number of frames produced and does not include the three information-panel sets.
The first actual reuse requires real return transport, inspection, and reinstallation rather than simply labelling the design 'reusable.'
Replacement of the foot pad shows that maintenance and available spare parts can be part of keeping a product in use.
Transport, cleaning, storage, labour, and other material inputs still need separate accounting; a lower frame count alone cannot establish an overall environmental or economic advantage.
mapping: Three new frames in the original plan → a linear approach in which each event begins with a newly made frame.
One frame used across three events → retention of product value through two actual return-and-reuse cycles.
Replacement of the worn foot pad → a specific maintenance and spare-parts action that enables continued use.
Three information-panel sets → content-specific components that are still produced separately and are not part of the frame 3→1 count change.
Return transport, cleaning, and storage → the operating system required to turn theoretical reusability into actual reuse.
module.boundary: Design for circularity does not mean reuse or recycling is always the preferred option in every situation, nor does a demountable product automatically become durable, safe, economical, or actually recovered. This example shows only that, across three same-specification events, one frame is actually used three times, including two reuse events after the initial use. Information panels, replacement parts, transport, cleaning, storage, and labour still require additional inputs. Without further life-cycle or cost analysis, the example cannot establish lower carbon emissions, lower total cost, zero pollution, or 100% recycling. Circular-economy principles are broader and also include eliminating waste and pollution, circulating products and materials, and regenerating nature; this article focuses only on the entry point of keeping a product in use.
module.reflection: Suppose the same frame has served two events, but the third venue changes its dimensions. Does previous reuse establish that it will fit the third event or have lower total environmental impact? What information is missing?

references.citation: Ellen MacArthur Foundation. (2024, August 21). Circular economy principles.
references.use: Supports the design-driven circular-economy principles of eliminating waste and pollution, circulating products and materials, and regenerating nature, and discusses maintaining, reusing, and refurbishing as ways to preserve product value. This article focuses only on actual reuse as an entry point and does not use the source to claim that the fictional display system achieves lower total impacts or lower cost.

references.citation: European Commission. (2020). Investing in the Circular Economy: A Blueprint for a Green Recovery. Publications Office of the European Union.
references.use: Supports maintaining product and material value through longer-lasting and repairable design and through reverse-logistics pathways for reuse and refurbishment. This policy factsheet is not used as empirical evidence for the fictional frame's costs, material quantities, energy use, or environmental performance.

articles.title: The Cuff That Stalled the Costume Change
articles.summaryZh: 演员要在几十秒内换好衣服，袖口却总卡在手掌上。方宁不想换掉已经定好的纱线，针织台边另一块同批纱线的试片，让她有了新的选择。
articles.summary: The actor has only a few dozen seconds to change costumes, but a cuff keeps catching on the hand. Fang Ning wants to keep the chosen yarn. Another swatch beside the knitting table suggests a different option.
storyParagraphsZh: 剧团正在改一件舞台上衣。演员只有几十秒换装，第一版袖口却刚好卡在手掌最宽的地方，每次都要停下来把布一点点往下拽。方宁已经和舞美确认过纱线的颜色与表面效果，不想为了这一处袖口把整件衣服的材料都换掉。
针织台边还留着用同一批纱线织出的另一种组织。方宁剪下两块宽度相同的试片，在两块布上各做两个原本相距100 mm的标记，再沿袖口实际会被撑开的同一方向比较。她把每块试片分别接到同一只小弹簧秤上，拉到同一个较小读数：第一块两标记间变成约112 mm，第二块到了约140 mm。
她把第二块布放到灯下，再慢慢拉一次。原本弯曲相连的线圈先转动、张开，彼此位置也在变化，布面就在这些几何变化中被拉长。100 mm到140 mm意味着这段布面的长度增加约40%，但这并不等于组成它的每根纱线本身都各自伸长了40%。方宁把刚翻开的纱线册合上，转而问针织师：“袖口能不能只换这个组织？”
新的小袖口装到试衣样衣上，演员把手掌顺利穿了过去。松手后，袖口回到当次试穿可用的尺寸。方宁看了看灯下更明显的织纹，把新组织只留在袖口，衣身仍保持原来平整的织面。
正式排练时，演员从上一套服装出来，抬手穿进新袖口，另一只手已经伸去拿下一件外套，没有再低头和袖口较劲。方宁站在侧幕边看见那只手顺利穿过去，便把原来那对卡手的旧袖口塞回工具篮，转身去管下一场换装。
storyParagraphs: The theatre company is altering a stage top. The actor has only a few dozen seconds to change costumes, but the first cuff catches at the widest part of the hand and has to be worked down little by little every time. Fang Ning has already agreed with the stage-design team on the yarn's colour and surface appearance, and she does not want to change the material for the entire garment just to solve one cuff.

Another knitted structure made from the same batch of yarn is still sitting beside the knitting table. Fang Ning cuts two specimens of the same width and places two marks on each, initially 100 mm apart. She compares them along the same direction in which the cuff would actually be stretched. Each specimen is connected in turn to the same small spring scale and pulled until the scale reaches the same low reading. The distance between the marks on the first specimen becomes about 112 mm; on the second, about 140 mm.

She places the second fabric under the light and slowly stretches it again. The curved, connected loops first rotate and open, while their relative positions also change, allowing the fabric surface to lengthen through these geometric changes. An increase from 100 mm to 140 mm means this measured length of fabric has increased by about 40%, but it does not mean that every yarn in the fabric has itself elongated by 40%. Fang Ning closes the yarn catalogue she has just opened and asks the knitter, “Can we change only the cuff to this structure?”

With the new cuff attached to the fitting garment, the actor’s hand passes through smoothly. After release, the cuff returns to a size usable for that fitting. Fang Ning looks at its more visible texture under the light and keeps the new structure at the cuff, leaving the garment’s body in the flatter original fabric.

During the full rehearsal, the actor comes out of the previous costume and pushes a hand through the new cuff while the other hand is already reaching for the next jacket. There is no need to stop and wrestle with the sleeve. Fang Ning, standing in the wings, has just enough time to see the hand pass through cleanly before she drops the old, tight cuffs back into the tool basket and turns to the next costume change.
articles.overallZh: 同样的纱线可以织成不同的线圈连接和排列方式，形成伸展表现不同的织物。受拉时，保持原有连接的线圈可以转动、张开、改变形状，使布面拉长。纱线自身的性质与织物的组织结构，是需要一起考虑的两个层次。
articles.overall: The same yarn can be knitted into different loop connections and arrangements, producing fabrics with different stretch behavior. Under a pull, loops can rotate, open, and change shape while retaining their connections, allowing the fabric to lengthen. Yarn properties and fabric structure are two levels that need to be considered together.
explanationParagraphsZh: 针织物的表现不仅取决于纤维和纱线本身，也取决于线圈怎样连接和排列。不同织法形成不同的组织；受拉时，既定连接下的线圈可以改变几何形状，增加布面长度。因此，织物伸长不等于每根纱线都按同样比例拉长。
最小核对：同一小拉力下，两块试片的原始标距都是100 mm；变成112 mm时增加12%，变成140 mm时增加40%。这两个比例描述布面两标记之间的变化，不是每根纱线的应变。数值是教学示意，不是论文数据或某类织物的通用伸长率。
explanationParagraphs: A knitted fabric’s behavior depends on the fibres and yarn, and also on how the loops connect and are arranged. Different stitch patterns create different structures. Under tension, loops within a given connected pattern can change geometry and increase fabric length. Fabric extension therefore does not mean that every yarn lengthens by the same proportion.

Minimal check: under the same small force, both specimens start with 100 mm between marks. Reaching 112 mm is a 12% increase; reaching 140 mm is a 40% increase. These percentages describe the marked fabric length, not the strain of every yarn. The values are teaching examples, not reported paper data or universal stretch values for a fabric type.

moduleZh.intro: 固定纱线来源、初始标距、拉伸方向和小拉力，只改变针织组织，观察布面长度如何不同。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 纱线相同，为什么两种针织组织还能伸得不一样
diagramSteps: 用同批纱线准备两种不同针织组织的同宽试片
在两块试片上分别设置原始相距100 mm的标记
沿同一方向用同一弹簧秤拉到同一个较小读数
两标记间分别变为约112 mm和140 mm
观察线圈转动与张开后，把袖口方案从换纱线改为换组织
diagramStepNotes: 同批纱线提供相同的原料来源信息；织物组织仍是另一层条件。
100 mm是两个标记之间的原始测量长度，不是整块试片总长。
弹簧秤读到相同的小拉力，方向也对应；这里并未要求两块拉到同一长度。
两段布面分别伸长12%和40%，不代表其中每根纱线也伸长相同比例。
新袖口通过当次试穿，纹路也更明显；长期回复性和耐久仍需另外判断。
mapping: 同一个纱线名称 → 相同原料层信息，但不足以决定织物层表现。
两种针织组织 → 不同的线圈连接方式和几何布置。
112 mm与140 mm → 同一小拉力下不同布面伸展的虚构教学结果。
更明显的袖口纹路 → 改变组织后付出的外观代价。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只说明同一纱线可以因针织组织和线圈几何不同而表现出不同伸展。实际织物还受纱线性质、线圈密度、整理、方向、载荷大小和循环历史等因素影响。织物伸长不能直接等同为纤维或每根纱线同等比例伸长；一次伸展也不能建立长期回复性、耐久性或其他成衣性能结论。
moduleZh.reflection: 另一块布的两标记原距80 mm，受拉后为100 mm，布面长度增加了多少百分比？能据此认定每根纱线也伸长相同比例吗？

module.intro: Hold yarn source, original gauge length, pulling direction, and small force constant, change the knitted structure, and observe how the fabric length responds differently.
module.diagramTitle: If the Yarn Is the Same, Why Can Two Knitted Structures Stretch Differently?
diagramSteps: Prepare two same-width specimens with different knitted structures using yarn from the same batch
Set two marks 100 mm apart on each specimen as the original measured length
Pull both in the same direction using the same spring scale to the same low reading
The marked distances become about 112 mm and 140 mm respectively
After observing loop rotation and opening, change the cuff solution from different yarn to different knitted structure
diagramStepNotes: The same yarn batch provides the same source-material information; fabric structure is another level of conditions.
The 100 mm is the original distance between two marks, not the specimen’s total length.
The spring scale reads the same small force in the corresponding direction. The specimens are not required to reach the same length.
The marked fabric lengths increase by 12% and 40%, not necessarily by the same proportions as every yarn within them.
The cuff works for this fitting and has a more visible texture; long-term recovery and durability need separate assessment.
mapping: Same yarn name → the same raw-material-level information, but not enough to determine fabric-level performance.
Two knitted structures → different loop connections and geometric arrangements.
112 mm and 140 mm → fictional teaching outcomes showing different fabric extension under the same small force.
More visible cuff texture → the appearance trade-off introduced by changing the structure.
module.boundary: This article only shows that the same yarn can produce different stretch behavior when knitted structure and loop geometry differ. Real fabrics are also affected by yarn properties, stitch density, finishing, direction, load magnitude, and loading history. Fabric extension cannot be equated directly with the same proportional extension of fibres or every yarn, and one stretch test does not establish long-term recovery, durability, or other garment properties.
module.reflection: Another fabric has 80 mm between two marks before loading and 100 mm afterward. What is the percentage increase in that fabric length? Does it establish that every yarn has extended by the same percentage?

referencesZh.citation: Singal, K., Dimitriyev, M. S., Gonzalez, S. E., Cachine, A. P., Quinn, S., & Matsumoto, E. A. (2024). Programming mechanics in knitted materials, stitch by stitch. Nature Communications, 15, 2622. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46498-z
referencesZh.use: 支持相同组成纱线通过改变针织线圈拓扑和几何可形成不同力学响应，并支持区分纱线层与织物结构层；不用于声称所有针织物都能完全回复、纱线从不伸长或其他成衣性能由组织单独决定。

references.citation: Singal, K., Dimitriyev, M. S., Gonzalez, S. E., Cachine, A. P., Quinn, S., & Matsumoto, E. A. (2024). Programming mechanics in knitted materials, stitch by stitch. Nature Communications, 15, 2622. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46498-z

It is not used to claim that all knitted fabrics recover perfectly, that yarn never stretches, or that stitch structure alone determines other garment properties.

articles.summaryZh: 一块大叶印花布只够做一件衬衫。林遥转动纸样，终于省出了余料，纸样上的箭头和侧缝上的叶子，却让她迟迟没有落剪。
storyParagraphsZh: 林遥要给服装画册做一件大叶印花衬衫，摄影师连背景颜色都已经按这块布定好了。主布展开后，她发现余量只够稳妥地裁这一套正式裁片，不能靠“先剪一版看看”再补救。最难摆的是一块细长侧片：按纸样原来的方向放，会剩下几条不好利用的窄边；转九十度，版面立刻宽松许多。
主布还是完整的，林遥只在上面移动纸样。这是一块机织印花布，已经铺平，经纬方向和直布边也事先核过。旋转后的侧片上，大叶图案看着没有倒置，可纸样中央那支标出材料取向的长箭头，已经不再与直布边平行。她量了箭头两端到同一条直布边的距离，一头近、一头远，于是把纸样转回规定取向，直到两端距离相同。
准备继续排其余纸样时，摄影助理指了指侧缝位置：“这两片叶子最后能接上吗？”林遥把相邻纸样按接合记号靠在一起。若只看纸样外侧的裁剪轮廓，叶尖像是正好相接；可真正缝合时，两边都会有一段布被收进缝份。她改看纸样标出的缝合位置，叶柄在那里反而错开了。
这一次，她没有再旋转纸样。侧片的纹向箭头继续保持与布边平行，只把整片纸样在布面上平移，旁边尚未裁下的纸样也跟着重新腾挪。林遥把相邻接合记号重新对上，再检查这条侧缝真正形成的位置，直到叶片在那里自然衔接。新的排法更费布，原本能留下的一大块整余料也被挤成了几块零碎区域。
林遥沿这一侧最后核对了纹向箭头、接合记号和缝合线，才落下剪刀。正式裁片只有这一套。缝好后到了拍摄日，模特转身，侧缝上的大叶从前片接到了后片。摄影师从取景器后说：“侧面这一张也留。”林遥把形状古怪的余布拢进材料袋，原本想顺手做的小配饰只好取消。
articles.overallZh: 排纸样时，材料方向和接缝图案要用不同参照核对。纹向箭头按设计要求对应布料方向；印花能否跨过接缝连续，则要看真正的缝合线和接合记号。裁剪边上的叶子碰在一起，并不能代替这两项检查。
explanationParagraphsZh: 纸样上的纹向箭头（grainline）标示这块裁片应按哪个材料方向摆放。在平整、直布边可用且经纬已核实的机织布上，若纸样要求直纹放置，箭头通常与布边平行。量箭头两端到同一条直布边的距离，两端相同，就能核对这个平行关系。
图案匹配是另一个问题。裁剪边会包含之后进入缝份的部分，所以两块裁边上的花纹看似相接，并不保证缝好后仍相接。应把相邻纸样按接合记号定位，并检查真正的缝合线附近图案。

moduleZh.intro: 先按纸样设计要求确定裁片的材料取向，再保持这个取向平移纸样，核对真正接缝处的印花。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 纸样方向对了以后，为什么图案还要在另一处重新核对
diagramSteps: 在经纬和直布边已核实的机织印花布上预排纸样，暂不下剪
按本例直纹设计要求，使纹向箭头两端到同一直布边的距离相同
保持这个取向，将相邻纸样按接合记号定位
检查实际缝合线附近的印花，而不只看裁剪边
必要时平移纸样并复查整体排料，再裁出这一套正式裁片
diagramStepNotes: 本例只针对已经确认经纬方向的机织布；印花朝向本身不能替代纱线方向判断。
纸样是否必须与布边平行应服从纸样设计意图；有意的斜裁或横纹布局并不是错误。
平移纸样不会改变grainline的方向，只改变纸样在布面上的位置。
图案匹配要看缝合线和相邻接合记号，因为裁剪边的一部分会进入缝份。
一条侧缝匹配成功不代表整件衣服所有花纹、合身、缩率或垂坠问题都自动解决。
mapping: 纸样长箭头 → 纸样规定的材料方向参照。
直布边 → 本例中检查grainline平行关系的稳定参照。
接合记号与缝合线 → 判断相邻裁片最终图案是否连续的位置。
减少的整块余料 → 同时满足材料方向和接缝图案要求所付出的排料代价。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只处理已核实经纬方向的机织印花布。grainline的具体方向应遵循纸样本身的设计要求，并非所有衣片都必须按同一种顺纹放置；斜裁和横纹布局可以是有意设计。印花方向也不等于经纬方向。正确的纹向和一条接缝上的图案匹配都不能单独保证整件成衣的合身、缩率、绒向或全部视觉连续性。
moduleZh.reflection: 另一张纸样明确要求斜裁，但转成箭头平行布边会让印花更好接。能只为拼图案就改变它的设计取向吗？材料方向与接缝图案应分别在哪里核对？

referencesZh.citation: SEWING.org. Understanding Pattern Markings, Part 1. Sewing Guideline 3.110 (document marked 5/07).
referencesZh.use: 支持grainline箭头用于纸样定位，并在纸样未另作指示时通常与布边平行；也支持图案匹配应依据缝合线和相邻接合记号，而不能只看裁剪边。

referencesZh.citation: SEWING.org. Preparing to Sew: What to Know Before You Sew—Fabric & Pattern Preparation. Sewing Guideline 4.104 (document marked 3/06).
referencesZh.use: 支持机织布经纬、布边和斜纹方向的基本区分，以及裁剪前核对布料纹向的重要性；本篇不采用其中关于针织或家庭处理的广泛说法。

articles.title: Before the First Cut
articles.summary: There is just enough large-leaf printed fabric for one shirt. Rotating a pattern piece frees up a useful remnant, but its arrow and the leaves at the side seam make Lin Yao hesitate before cutting.
storyParagraphs: Lin Yao is making a large-leaf printed shirt for a fashion catalogue, and the photographer has already chosen the background colour around this fabric. Once the main fabric is spread out, she realizes there is only enough material to cut one reliable final set of pieces; she cannot afford to “cut one version and see” before trying again. The hardest piece to place is a long, narrow side panel. In the pattern's original orientation it leaves several narrow strips that are difficult to use, but rotating it ninety degrees immediately makes the layout much easier.

The main fabric is still uncut; Lin Yao is only moving the paper patterns. This is a woven printed fabric, laid flat, with its warp, weft and straight selvage already checked. The large leaves on the rotated side panel do not look upside down, but the long arrow marking the pattern’s intended material direction is no longer parallel to the selvage. She measures from both ends of the arrow to that same edge. One end is closer, so she rotates the pattern back to its specified orientation until the distances are equal.

As she prepares to place the remaining pattern pieces, the photography assistant points toward the side seam. “Will these two leaves actually meet?” Lin Yao brings the adjoining paper pieces together using their matching notches. If she looks only at the outer cutting outlines, the leaf tips seem to meet perfectly. But when the garment is sewn, part of the fabric on both sides will disappear into the seam allowance. She looks instead at the seamlines marked on the patterns, and there the leaf stems are offset.

This time she does not rotate the pattern again. The side panel's grainline arrow stays parallel to the selvage; she only slides the entire pattern piece across the fabric, while the neighboring pieces that have not yet been cut are shifted around to make room. Lin Yao realigns the adjoining notches and checks the position where this side seam will actually form until the leaves connect naturally there. The new layout uses more fabric, and the large continuous remnant she could have saved earlier is squeezed into several smaller irregular areas.

Lin Yao checks the grainline arrow, matching notches and seamline along this side one last time, then lowers the scissors. This is the only final set of pieces she cuts. Once the shirt is sewn and the photography day arrives, the model turns and a large leaf continues across the side seam from front to back. “Keep this side shot too,” the photographer says from behind the viewfinder. Lin Yao gathers the oddly shaped scraps into the material bag. The small accessory she had hoped to make has to be dropped.
articles.overall: Laying out a pattern requires two different reference checks. The grainline arrow follows the design’s intended material direction; print continuity across adjoining pieces is checked at the actual seamline and matching notches. Leaf tips meeting at the cut edges cannot replace those checks.
explanationParagraphs: The grainline arrow on a paper pattern indicates the intended material direction of that piece. On flat woven fabric with a usable straight selvage and verified warp and weft, a piece intended for straight-grain placement normally has its arrow parallel to the selvage. Measuring equal distances from both ends of the arrow to that same edge checks this parallel relationship.

Pattern matching is a separate issue. Cut edges include material that will later disappear into seam allowances, so prints that seem to meet at the cutting edges may not meet after sewing. Adjoining pattern pieces should be positioned using their matching notches, and the print should be checked around the actual seamline.

module.intro: First establish the material orientation required by the pattern, then slide pieces without rotating them to check the print at the actual seam.
module.diagramTitle: Once the Pattern Orientation Is Correct, Why Must the Print Still Be Checked Somewhere Else?
diagramSteps: Lay out paper patterns on woven printed fabric with checked warp, weft and straight selvage, without cutting yet
For this straight-grain design, place both ends of the grainline arrow the same distance from the same straight selvage
Keep that orientation and position adjoining pieces using their matching notches
Check the print around the actual seamline rather than only at cut edges
Slide pieces if needed, recheck the full layout, then cut the one final set of pieces
diagramStepNotes: This example applies only to woven fabric whose warp and weft directions have already been verified; print direction itself cannot substitute for yarn-direction information.
Whether a pattern piece should run parallel to the selvage depends on the pattern's design intent; deliberate bias or cross-grain layouts are not errors.
Sliding the pattern piece changes its position on the fabric without changing its grainline orientation.
Pattern matching should be checked at the seamline and adjoining notches because part of the cut edge will disappear into the seam allowance.
Successfully matching one side seam does not guarantee that every print, fit, shrinkage, nap, or drape issue in the whole garment is automatically resolved.
mapping: Long arrow on the paper pattern → the material-direction reference specified by the pattern.
Straight selvage → the stable reference used in this example to check grainline parallelism.
Matching notches and seamline → the locations used to judge whether adjoining pieces will produce continuous print at the finished seam.
Loss of a large usable remnant → the material-layout cost of satisfying both grain orientation and seam-pattern requirements.
module.boundary: This article applies only to woven printed fabric whose warp and weft directions have been verified. The specific grainline direction should follow the pattern's design intent; not every pattern piece must be placed on the same straight grain, and bias or cross-grain layouts can be intentional. Print direction is also not the same as warp/weft direction. Correct grain orientation and successful print matching at one seam do not by themselves guarantee overall garment fit, shrinkage behavior, nap handling, or complete visual continuity.
module.reflection: Another pattern explicitly calls for bias cutting, but rotating it parallel to the selvage would make the print easier to match. Is print matching alone a reason to change the intended orientation? Where should material direction and seam-print continuity each be checked?

references.citation: SEWING.org. Understanding Pattern Markings, Part 1. Sewing Guideline 3.110 (document marked 5/07).
references.use: Supports using the grainline arrow to position pattern pieces and, unless the pattern directs otherwise, keeping it parallel to the selvage. It also supports matching patterns by seamlines and adjoining notches rather than relying only on cut edges.

references.citation: SEWING.org. Preparing to Sew: What to Know Before You Sew—Fabric & Pattern Preparation. Sewing Guideline 4.104 (document marked 3/06).
references.use: Supports the basic distinction among warp, weft, selvage, and bias directions in woven fabric, as well as the importance of checking fabric grain before cutting. This article does not use the guide's broader claims about knits or household fabric-treatment practices.

articles.summaryZh: 门店明早要摆出新帆布袋，程璐今晚得确认陈列卡上的材料批次。供应商证书就在手边，却没说清这60只袋子怎样到了北店。
storyParagraphsZh: 第二天一早，两家门店都要把新到的帆布袋摆上主题陈列台。北店已经收到了60只，只差把材料批次写进旁边的小卡片，店员却在下班前发来一句：“这60只按我们的记录，真的能追到纱线批A吗？”程璐负责今晚给出答案，否则那张卡先不印。
材料档案里确实有供应商交来的证书，纱线批号A也写得清楚。程璐原本已经准备回复，却在发送前停住：那份证书说明上游提交了什么材料证据，却没有告诉她北店面前这60只后来经过哪一卷布、在哪一次裁剪中被拆分出来，又经过哪次交接到了门店。
她先找到北店收货单，这60只的成品组号是G2。夹在出库记录后的裁剪单写着布卷R1，织造记录又把R1接到纱线批A。程璐把单据按时间铺开，手边终于不再只有一张上游证书。她接着翻出同一布卷的拆分记录，看看剩下的货去了哪里。
同一卷布还形成G1的40只，交给东店；G2的60只交北店。两次交接和两家签收都对得上，40加60也与这次记录的100只相符。程璐把原来共用的材料说明分成两张，北店那张写：“按现有记录，本组成品G2关联布卷R1、纱线批A。”东店那张换成G1。打印晚了半小时，但两张卡终于各自跟上了自己的货。
关库前，打印机吐出最后两张陈列卡。程璐把北店那张夹在G2出库单上，东店那张放进第二天的文件袋。供应商证书仍留在材料档案里；只是这一次，卡片上写的是记录真正支持到哪一步，而不是把一张证书扩写成它没有回答的问题。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一组完整的虚构批次记录说明供应链可追溯性的一个入口：给材料、半成品和成品设置可关联身份，并记录转化、拆分、交接和去向后，可以沿记录从成品向后查输入，也可以从材料向前查可能去向。追溯回答的是记录链覆盖到哪里，不等同于对记录真实性、材料物理来源、环境或劳工表现的独立验证。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例只追踪记录所覆盖的R1分支，并假定R1只用纱线批A、拆分与交接记录完整。向后：北店60只属于G2，G2接到R1，再接到A。向前：在这条分支中，R1形成G1的40只和G2的60只，分别交东店和北店，共100只。这不穷尽A批可能的其他去向；成品数量相符有助于检查记录自洽，也不自行证明记录真实。
混合、身份保存和质量平衡监管链模型需要区分。若A、B两批混合且投入、转化和去向都有记录，仍可追到可能输入与输出集合；不能据此确定某件成品中每根纤维来自哪批。缺少交接、未记录混合或记录粒度不足时，应标明具体缺口及不能支持的归属，不把整条已知链一概抹去，也不自动补上未知部分。证书和编号须配合适当核验，才可支持更广的实质声明。

moduleZh.intro: 从一批具体成品向后追输入，再从材料批次向前追去向，并把每一步限制在实际存在的身份、拆分和交接记录上。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么一张供应商证书还不足以回答北店这60只具体来自哪一批
diagramSteps: 从北店收货记录确认60只成品属于批次G2
沿G2的裁剪记录向后找到布卷R1，再由R1记录关联到纱线批A
从纱线批A向前查看本例覆盖的布卷R1分支及其后续拆分
核对R1形成G1共40只交东店、G2共60只交北店，合计100只且交接记录连续
只在记录支持的范围内表达批次关联，并把材料真实性或环境劳工声明留给独立核验
diagramStepNotes: 追溯起点是具体门店收到的具体成品组，而不是泛化的供应商名单。
本例明确R1只用A，因此可以建立R1与A之间的记录身份关联。
向前追溯回答材料批次可能去了哪里，与从成品向后查来源方向相反。
40+60=100只是这次虚构成品拆分的数量核对，不是物料质量平衡，也不验证记录真假。
交接缺失、未记录混合或数据不可靠时，只将受影响环节或归属留为未知；保留已有证据支持的链路，不由系统自动补齐缺口。
mapping: G2的60只 → 从北店向后追溯的具体成品批次。
R1 → 把上游纱线批与下游两组成品连接起来的布卷身份。
G1的40只与G2的60只 → R1拆分后的两个已记录去向。
供应商证书 → 可作为其他证据，但不能代替具体批次转化与交接链。
两张门店陈列卡 → 把对外表达限制在现有记录真正支持的范围。
moduleZh.boundary: 可追溯性只覆盖被记录并能够可靠关联的范围。记录可能缺失、错误或被伪造；数量核对也不等于物理身份保存。混合批次、质量平衡或其他链条模型需要明确各自粒度，不能由账面数量推断某件产品中每根纤维的精确来源。追溯、供应链透明度、证书和对环境、劳工或地点表现的独立验证是互补但不同的工作。隐私和商业信息应按目的与角色管理，本篇也不要求全部供应链档案公开。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果北店的60只、东店的40只在数量上正好合计100只，但中间缺少R1到G2的一次交接记录，为什么不能仅凭数量闭合就把那一段来源自动补上？

referencesZh.citation: OECD. (2025, February 11). The role of sustainability certifications in due diligence in the garment and footwear sector. OECD Business and Finance Policy Papers, No. 77. OECD Publishing. https://doi.org/10.1787/ac8179f2-en
referencesZh.use: 支持服装与鞋类供应链中不同认证具有不同范围与可靠性，并不应仅依赖认证完成尽职调查；本篇因此保留供应商证书作为一种证据，但不让它替代具体批次追溯或独立验证实质声明。

referencesZh.citation: OECD/IEA. (2025, February 28). The role of traceability in critical mineral supply chains. OECD Publishing. https://doi.org/10.1787/edb0a451-en
referencesZh.use: 支持区分追溯、供应链映射、披露和不同监管链模型，并强调数据质量与验证；本篇借用这些跨行业概念说明身份保存与质量平衡不能混同，不把该矿产报告当作纺织材料性能数据。

articles.title: The Line on the Display Card
articles.summary: The store will display its new canvas bags tomorrow, and Cheng Lu must confirm the material-batch line tonight. The supplier certificate is at hand, but it does not show how these 60 bags reached the North Store.
storyParagraphs: Both stores are due to put their newly arrived canvas bags on themed display tables early the next morning. The North Store has already received 60 bags and only needs the material batch added to the small card beside them, but before closing the shop assistant sends one question: “According to our records, can these 60 really be traced back to yarn batch A?” Cheng Lu is responsible for giving an answer that evening; otherwise, the card will not be printed yet.

The material file does contain a certificate supplied by the vendor, and yarn batch A is clearly listed. Cheng Lu has almost finished drafting her reply when she stops before sending it. The certificate shows what evidence was submitted upstream, but it does not tell her which fabric roll these 60 bags in the North Store later came through, in which cutting split they were separated, or through which handover they reached the store.

She first finds the North Store’s receipt: these 60 bags carry finished-group number G2. The cutting sheet behind the dispatch record names fabric roll R1, and its weaving record links R1 to yarn batch A. Cheng Lu lays the documents out in time order. She now has more than an upstream certificate. Next she finds the split record for the same roll to see where the other goods went.

The same roll also yields 40 bags in G1 for the East Store; the 60 in G2 go north. Both handovers and receipts match, and 40 plus 60 matches the 100 finished bags in this record. Cheng Lu replaces the shared material statement with two cards. The North Store’s reads, “According to existing records, this finished group G2 links to fabric roll R1 and yarn batch A.” The East Store’s names G1 instead. Printing is half an hour late, but each card now follows its own goods.

Before the warehouse closes, the printer produces the final two display cards. Cheng Lu clips the North Store's card to the G2 dispatch record and puts the East Store's card into the next morning's document pouch. The supplier certificate remains in the material file; the difference is that this time, the cards state only what the records actually support rather than expanding one certificate into answers it never provided.
articles.overall: This article uses a complete fictional set of batch records to introduce one aspect of supply-chain traceability: when materials, intermediates, and finished goods have linkable identities and records of transformation, splitting, handover, and destination, records can be followed backward from finished goods to inputs and forward from a material batch to its possible destinations. Traceability answers how far the record chain reaches; it is not the same as independent verification of record truthfulness, physical material origin, or environmental or labour performance.
explanationParagraphs: This example follows only the R1 branch covered by the records and assumes that R1 uses only yarn batch A, with complete split and handover records. Backward: the North Store’s 60 bags belong to G2, which links to R1 and then A. Forward within this branch, R1 yields 40 bags in G1 and 60 in G2 for the East and North Stores, totaling 100. This does not exhaust other possible destinations of batch A. Matching finished-product counts helps check internal consistency but does not prove that the records are true.

Mixing, identity preservation and mass-balance chain-of-custody models are distinct. When batches A and B are mixed and their inputs, transformation and destinations are recorded, possible input and output sets can still be traced. That does not identify the source batch of every fibre in an individual item. A missing handover, unrecorded mixing or insufficient granularity calls for identifying the specific gap and unsupported attribution, rather than erasing known links or automatically filling unknown ones. Certificates and identifiers need appropriate verification to support broader substantive claims.

module.intro: Trace backward from a specific finished batch to its inputs, then trace forward from the material batch to its destinations, keeping every step within the identities, splits, and handover records that actually exist.

diagramSteps: Use the North Store receiving record to confirm that the 60 finished bags belong to batch G2
Follow G2's cutting record backward to fabric roll R1, then use the R1 record to link to yarn batch A

Confirm that R1 produced G1 with 40 bags for the East Store and G2 with 60 bags for the North Store, for 100 bags in total with continuous handover records
State batch relationships only within the scope supported by the records, and leave material authenticity or environmental and labour claims to independent verification
diagramStepNotes: The traceability starting point is a specific finished-goods group received by a specific store, not a general supplier list.
This example explicitly states that R1 uses only A, allowing a record-level identity link between R1 and A.
Forward tracing asks where a material batch may have gone and runs in the opposite direction from tracing finished goods backward to their source.
40+60=100 bags reconciles the finished-product count in this fictional split record. It is not a material mass balance or proof that the records are truthful.
When handovers are missing, mixing is unrecorded or data is unreliable, leave the affected link or attribution unknown while retaining supported links; do not fill gaps automatically.

R1 → the fabric-roll identity linking the upstream yarn batch to the two downstream finished-goods groups.
G1's 40 bags and G2's 60 bags → the two recorded destinations created when R1 was split.
Supplier certificate → evidence that may support other claims but cannot replace the specific batch-transformation and handover chain.
Two store display cards → outward-facing statements limited to what the existing records actually support.
module.boundary: Traceability covers only the scope that is recorded and can be reliably linked. Records may be missing, incorrect, or falsified, and quantity reconciliation is not the same as physical identity preservation. Mixed batches, mass-balance systems, and other chain-of-custody models require their own stated granularity and cannot use accounting quantities to infer the exact origin of every fibre in an individual product. Traceability, supply-chain transparency, certification, and independent verification of environmental, labour, or site performance are complementary but distinct activities. Privacy and commercial information should be managed according to purpose and role; this article does not require all supply-chain records to be public.
module.reflection: If the North Store's 60 bags and the East Store's 40 bags add up to exactly 100, but one handover record between R1 and G2 is missing, why can the missing provenance link not be filled in automatically from the quantity balance alone?

articles.summaryZh: 化验单还是0.8%，铲车也已等在进料仓前。沈舟本想让这批料直接上皮带，下午送来的回收测试却让他重新拿起计算器。
storyParagraphsZh: 夜班交接时，处理厂还有一段空余能力。沈舟要决定一批已经从矿下运到厂里的含铜物料今晚要不要直接上皮带；铲车停在进料仓前，司机等他一个手势。化验单仍是0.8%，和最近几批顺利处理的物料差不多，本来这应该是个很快的决定。
此前相似物料的回收率估计约为80%，下午这次测试却只有约50%。品位没变，每吨里原本含有的铜量仍一样，估计能回收到的铜却少了。材料已经采出，今晚处理线又有闲置能力。沈舟拿出计算器，要先看这一吨进流程所增加的净回收价值，能不能抵上相关处理费用。
一吨是1000 kg，0.8%含铜就是8 kg。沈舟先按80%回收，在纸上写下6.4 kg；再按每公斤10个账面单位的净回收价值，得到64。与处理这一吨直接相关的增量费用是50，64减50，还剩14。按此前这组条件，0.8%在账面上还能越过处理门槛。
沈舟把回收率换成刚拿到的约50%。同样8 kg含铜，现在估计只能回收4 kg，净回收价值变成40；再减去50的相关增量费用，就是负10。司机从驾驶室探出头：“进仓吗？”沈舟摇手：“先去待处理区。等这批的回收情况再确认。”化验单上的0.8%没变，车头却换了方向。
铲车沿黄线绕过进料仓，把物料卸到旁边的指定区域。沈舟转身去看下一批夜班调度。处理线那段空余能力暂时还空着，这一车物料也仍留在厂里；等新的回收信息出来，它还可以重新进入判断。
articles.overallZh: 边界品位是在给定条件下用来作取舍判断的品位门槛。本例只问：已经采出的物料，在处理线有闲置能力时，含铜量至少多少，才能让净回收价值抵上本次相关增量费用？回收率、净价值或费用改变，这个处理门槛也会改变。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本模型的处理阈值，是每吨物料的净回收价值刚好抵上相关增量费用时的含铜品位。计算时，品位用小数表示：0.8%代入0.008。每吨含铜量为品位×1000 kg/t，再乘回收率和每公斤的净回收价值，最后减去每吨相关增量费用。物料已采出，模型不重计已经发生的采矿成本；处理能力闲置，也不计挤走其他物料的产能机会成本。
固定每公斤净回收价值为10个账面单位、每吨相关增量费用为50个单位。80%回收时，阈值为50÷(1000×0.80×10)=0.00625，即0.625%；50%回收时为50÷(1000×0.50×10)=0.01，即1.0%。0.8%因而在前者之上、后者之下。两种费用口径不得重复：50是尚未计入每公斤净价值的本次相关增量处理费用。这些数字均为教学虚构。

moduleZh.intro: 先把化验品位换成每吨含有的金属量，再乘回收率得到可回收量，最后与本次决策相关的增量价值和费用比较。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 同样0.8%的物料，为什么回收率改变后会跨过处理门槛
diagramSteps: 已采物料1 t=1000 kg，0.8%品位对应8 kg含铜量
按80%回收，6.4 kg×10个账面单位/kg=64个单位净回收价值
扣除50个单位/t的相关增量处理费用，边际结果为+14
若当前回收估计降到50%，4 kg×10=40，扣50后变为-10
在同一固定假设下反推，80%回收时阈值为0.625%，50%回收时阈值为1.0%
diagramStepNotes: 0.8%先写成0.008；0.008×1000 kg得到每吨物料含铜8 kg。本例物料已采出。
8 kg×80%=6.4 kg，再乘净价值10个单位/kg。10是教学假设，不是真实铜价。
每吨只比较尚未计入净价值的相关增量处理费用50；闲置产能下，本模型未加挤走其他物料的机会成本。
新回收估计令可回收量降到4 kg，40-50=-10；测试代表性仍需确认，50%不是永久性质。
用费用除以每单位小数品位对应的回收价值；0.00625=0.625%，0.01=1.0%。
mapping: 0.8%化验品位 → 每吨原始物料中约8 kg含铜量。
80%与50%回收率 → 把相同含铜量转换成不同可回收量。
+14与-10 → 在同一净价值和相关增量费用假设下的不同边际处理结果。
铲车转向待处理区 → 当前条件下暂不处理，而非对物料永久分类。
moduleZh.boundary: 这是已采材料、存在闲置处理能力、单金属、固定净回收价值和固定相关增量费用下的简化边际处理模型。若存在处理能力瓶颈、其他物料的机会成本、额外运输或重新开采费用、多个有价元素、价格变化或其他约束，阈值会不同。这里的边际处理结果不是全矿利润、项目估值、储量认证或投资建议，所有数字均为教学虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 仍按回收率50%、每公斤净价值10个账面单位、每吨相关增量费用50计算，若品位为1.2%，每吨边际余量是多少？这个结果为什么仍不能当作全矿利润？

referencesZh.citation: CIM Mineral Resource and Mineral Reserve Committee. (2019, November 29). CIM Estimation of Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves Best Practice Guidelines. Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum.
referencesZh.use: 支持边界品位需要在明确条件和时间下定义，并区分盈亏平衡、弃置及运营/边际阈值；也支持把成本、回收率和价格等作为阈值输入。本篇只采用已采物料、闲置产能和相关增量费用的简化处理决策，不把它扩展为完整项目盈利或储量认证。

articles.title: A Different Turn at the Feed Bin
articles.summary: The assay still reads 0.8%, and the loader is waiting at the feed bin. Shen Zhou is about to send the batch onto the conveyor when an afternoon recovery test makes him reach for the calculator again.
storyParagraphs: At the night-shift handover, the processing plant still has some spare capacity. Shen Zhou must decide whether a batch of copper-bearing material that has already been mined and delivered to the plant should go directly onto the conveyor tonight. The loader is waiting in front of the feed bin for his signal. The assay still reads 0.8%, similar to several recent batches that were processed without hesitation, so this would normally be a quick decision.

Similar material had previously been estimated at about 80% recovery, but the afternoon test gives only about 50%. The grade is unchanged, so each tonne still contains the same amount of copper; less of it is now expected to be recovered. The material is already mined, and the processing line has spare capacity tonight. Shen Zhou takes out his calculator to see whether the net recoverable value added by processing this tonne will cover the relevant cost.

One tonne is 1000 kg, so 0.8% means 8 kg of contained copper. Shen Zhou first uses 80% recovery and writes down 6.4 kg. At a net recoverable value of 10 accounting units per kilogram, that gives 64. The incremental cost directly associated with processing this tonne is 50, leaving 14. Under those earlier conditions, 0.8% still sits above the processing threshold.

Shen Zhou replaces the recovery estimate with the new figure of about 50%. The same 8 kg of contained copper would now yield an estimated 4 kg recovered, giving 40 accounting units of net value. Subtract the 50 units of relevant incremental cost and the result is -10. The driver leans out of the cab. “Into the bin?” Shen Zhou waves him off. “Take it to the holding area for now. We’ll wait until the recovery picture for this batch is clearer.” The assay still says 0.8%, but the loader turns the other way.

The loader follows the yellow line around the feed bin and unloads the material in the designated area nearby. Shen Zhou turns to the next item on the night-shift schedule. That section of processing capacity remains unused for the moment, and the material is still at the plant; when new recovery information arrives, it can be evaluated again.
articles.overall: Cut-off grade is a grade threshold used to make a decision under specified conditions. This example asks only how much copper already mined material must contain for its net recoverable value to cover the relevant incremental cost when the processing plant has spare capacity. Change recovery, net value or cost, and that processing threshold changes too.
explanationParagraphs: In this model, the processing threshold is the copper grade at which net recoverable value per tonne just covers the relevant incremental cost. Enter grade as a decimal: 0.8% becomes 0.008. Multiply grade by 1000 kg/t to obtain contained copper per tonne, then by recovery and net value per kilogram. Subtract the relevant incremental cost per tonne. The material is already mined, so mining costs already incurred are not counted again. Spare capacity also means the model includes no capacity opportunity cost for displacing other material.

Fix net recoverable value at 10 accounting units per kilogram and relevant incremental cost at 50 units per tonne. At 80% recovery, the threshold is 50÷(1000×0.80×10)=0.00625, or 0.625%. At 50% recovery it is 50÷(1000×0.50×10)=0.01, or 1.0%. The grade of 0.8% therefore lies above the first threshold and below the second. The cost categories must not overlap: the 50 units are relevant incremental processing costs not already included in the net value per kilogram. All values are fictional teaching assumptions.

module.intro: Convert assay grade into contained metal per tonne, apply recovery to obtain recoverable metal, and then compare the resulting incremental value with the incremental cost relevant to this processing decision.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can the Same 0.8% Material Cross the Processing Threshold When Recovery Changes?
diagramSteps: For already mined material, 1 t=1000 kg and a grade of 0.8% corresponds to 8 kg of contained copper
At 80% recovery, 6.4 kg×10 accounting units/kg=64 units of net recoverable value
Subtract 50 units/t of relevant incremental processing cost to obtain a marginal result of +14
If the current recovery estimate falls to 50%, 4 kg×10=40 and subtracting 50 gives -10
Under the same fixed assumptions, the threshold is 0.625% at 80% recovery and 1.0% at 50% recovery
diagramStepNotes: Write 0.8% as 0.008: 0.008×1000 kg gives 8 kg of contained copper per tonne. This material is already mined.
8 kg×80%=6.4 kg, then multiply by 10 units/kg of net value. The 10 is a teaching assumption, not a real copper price.
Compare the 50 units/t of relevant incremental processing cost not already included in net value. With spare capacity, this model adds no opportunity cost for displacing other material.
The new recovery estimate gives 4 kg recovered and 40-50=-10. Test representativeness still matters; 50% is not a permanent property.
Divide cost by the recoverable value per unit of decimal grade: 0.00625=0.625% and 0.01=1.0%.
mapping: 0.8% assay grade → about 8 kg of contained copper per tonne of original material.
80% versus 50% recovery → conversion of the same contained metal into different recoverable amounts.
+14 versus -10 → different marginal processing results under the same net-value and incremental-cost assumptions.
Loader sent to the holding area → a decision not to process under current conditions, not a permanent classification of the material.
module.boundary: This is a simplified marginal processing model for already mined material, spare processing capacity, a single metal, fixed net recoverable value, and fixed relevant incremental cost. If processing capacity is constrained, other material has an opportunity cost, extra transport or remine costs arise, multiple valuable elements are present, prices change, or other constraints apply, the threshold will change. The marginal processing result here is not whole-mine profit, project valuation, reserve certification, or investment advice. All numerical values are fictional teaching assumptions.
module.reflection: Keeping 50% recovery, 10 accounting units/kg of net value and 50 units/t of relevant incremental cost, what is the marginal result per tonne at a grade of 1.2%? Why is that result still not whole-mine profit?

references.citation: CIM Mineral Resource and Mineral Reserve Committee. (2019, November 29). CIM Estimation of Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves Best Practice Guidelines. Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum.
references.use: Supports defining cut-off grade under specified conditions and at a specified time, distinguishing break-even, discard, and operational or marginal thresholds, and using inputs such as cost, recovery, and price. This article uses only a simplified processing decision for already mined material with spare capacity and relevant incremental costs; it does not extend the example into complete project profitability or reserve certification.

articles.summaryZh: 林珂准备提交矿料采购意见，一份合作社已经支付的清理费用记录送进了会议室。原来的采购表上没有这一行。
storyParagraphsZh: 材料工作室要为下一季样品订矿物原料，林珂负责交采购意见。这批材料对工作室最多值100个计价单位，供应方报价也正好是100；生产者已为它耗用了70单位的劳动、设备和其他资源。会议开始时，大家准备继续谈合同条件。
林珂正要合上采购表，一份新记录被送进会议室。附近用水合作社已经为清理受影响的取水设施付了40单位。报告把这项损害与同一次开采联系起来，费用没有得到补偿，也不在生产者那70单位资源成本里。
她把两项成本分开写在纸上。70是生产者自己为了取得这批材料耗用的资源；40却由没有参加这笔矿料买卖的合作社承担。如果只盯着100的报价，这40根本不会自动出现在买卖双方的账上。林珂于是把原先准备直接进入议价的下一步停下来，让团队先把第三方损害也放进同一张比较表。
采购讨论没有按原计划结束。林珂先注明：这批矿料已经生产，清理费也已经付出，现在不买并不能让那70和40消失。这一页记录要补齐的是该批开采影响的回顾性账目；若继续订下一批，团队还得另查未来会增加或可以避免的成本。她把这两项待核查内容留在采购表旁，交期因此往后推。
散会后，林珂把原来的采购表从打印机旁拿回来，在70下面另加一行“第三方未补偿清理损害：40”。100的报价仍写在最上面。她没有在表角写“必须买”或“必须停”，只是把更新后的版本夹回文件夹，让下一轮讨论从一张更完整的账开始。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一笔简化矿物交易说明开采外部性的一个入口：开采活动可能给未直接参与相关交易的第三方带来影响，而这些影响没有充分进入买卖双方承担的成本或收益时，就会形成交易价格之外的重要成本。负外部性只是外部性的一种，个案是否存在以及大小仍需要证据支持。
explanationParagraphsZh: 对这批已生产矿料设一个完整情景：假设最终完成交换，并实现买方支付意愿所代表的100单位价值，成交价也恰为100。已发生的生产资源成本70不含第三方清理损害40，且假定没有其他效应。价值减生产资源耗用为100−70=30；计入不重合的损害后为100−(70+40)=−10。这是该假设完成情景的净额，不是尚未成交时已经实现的历史收益，也不是说现在不买就能收回已发生的70和40。
如果按100成交，这笔支付是在买卖双方之间转移，不应再加成另一项社会资源成本。社会账比较的是假设实现的价值、真实资源耗用与第三方损害；未来订单则需另评估可避免的增量影响。100、70、40及损害归因都是教学设定，不是现实矿址数据，也不代表40已经包括全部生态价值。

moduleZh.intro: 先把交易参与方自己承担的资源成本与交易外第三方承担的损害分开，再看后者是否已经进入原来的交易判断。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么报价仍是100，第三方的40单位损害却会改变整体比较
diagramSteps: 假设已产出矿料最终成交，并实现买方100单位价值，成交价也为100
记录生产者实际耗用资源成本70，并明确其中不含第三方损害
识别案例中已建立因果关联、由交易外用水合作社承担且未获补偿的40单位清理损害
把生产资源成本与第三方损害合计为70+40=110，而不是把价格100再作为额外资源成本加入
在这一假设完成情景中计算100−110=−10；当前或未来决策另查可避免的增量影响
diagramStepNotes: 100是本例假设完成交易并实现的买方价值，不是尚未成交时已实现的收益，也不是任何价格都等于社会价值。
70包括生产者耗用的劳动、设备等资源，但明确排除同一项40单位第三方损害。
40只有在案例证据已支持与该开采活动存在因果关联的前提下才能这样计入；现实个案不能仅凭空间邻近归因。
价格100是买方支付给卖方的转移，不应在社会资源成本中与70和40重复相加。
−10以实现100价值且没有其他效应为条件；已发生的成本与未来可避免成本须分开，不据此决定关矿或最优政策。
mapping: 买方价值100 → 假设交易最终完成并实现的价值，不是已成交事实。
生产资源成本70 → 生产者为取得该批材料实际耗用的资源，不含第三方40。
合作社清理损害40 → 未参与交易的第三方承担且未获补偿的外部成本。
采购表新增一行 → 将原先遗漏在交易双方账外的已识别成本带回决策比较。
moduleZh.boundary: 现实中的水质或设施损害可能来自自然背景、历史遗留污染、其他设施或时间变化，因此必须有合适的源头、时间、对照和其他证据才能进行个案归因。矿山酸性排水等机制也依矿物、氧气、水和场址条件而异，并非所有矿山必然发生。本篇的100、70和40及其因果关系均为虚构已知条件；不能据此判断任何真实矿址的责任、赔偿、最优税率、关闭决策或全部生态价值。某项影响暂时无法可靠货币化，也不意味着它的价值必然为零。

articles.title: Who Paid the Forty?
articles.summary: Lin Ke is about to submit a mineral-procurement recommendation when a record of a water cooperative’s already-paid cleanup bill reaches the meeting. Her procurement sheet has no line for it.
storyParagraphs: A materials studio needs mineral inputs for next season’s samples, and Lin Ke has to submit a procurement recommendation. The batch is worth at most 100 accounting units to the studio, matching the supplier’s quote. The producer has already used 70 units of labour, equipment and other resources to obtain it. The meeting is ready to move on to contract terms.

Lin Ke is about to close the procurement sheet when a new record arrives. A nearby water cooperative has already spent 40 units cleaning an affected intake facility. The report links that damage to the same extraction activity. The bill has not been compensated and is not part of the producer’s 70 units of resource cost.

She writes the two costs separately on the page. The 70 is the resource use borne by the producer in obtaining the batch; the 40 falls on a cooperative that did not participate in the mineral transaction. If the team looks only at the quoted price of 100, the 40 will never automatically appear in the buyer's or seller's accounts. Lin Ke therefore pauses the planned move directly into price negotiation and asks the team to place the third-party damage into the same comparison.

The procurement discussion does not end on schedule. Lin Ke first notes that this batch has already been produced and the cleanup bill paid: declining to buy now would not make the 70 or 40 disappear. This page completes a retrospective account of the batch’s extraction impacts. For another order, the team would need separate evidence about future additional or avoidable costs. She leaves both questions beside the procurement sheet, delaying the timetable.

After the meeting, Lin Ke picks up the original procurement sheet from beside the printer and adds a separate line beneath the 70: “Uncompensated third-party cleanup damage: 40.” The quoted price of 100 remains at the top. She does not write “must buy” or “must stop” in the corner; she simply returns the updated version to the folder so that the next discussion begins from a more complete account.
articles.overall: This article uses a simplified mineral transaction to introduce one aspect of extraction externalities: extraction activity may impose effects on third parties who do not directly participate in the transaction, and when those effects are not adequately reflected in the costs or benefits considered by the buyer and seller, they become important costs outside the transaction price. Negative externalities are only one form of externality, and whether a particular case exists and how large it is still requires evidence.
explanationParagraphs: Consider a complete scenario for the already-produced batch: suppose exchange is eventually completed and the value represented by willingness to pay is realized at 100 units, with a transaction price also of 100. Incurred production resource cost is 70, excluding the third-party cleanup damage of 40, and no other effects are assumed. Value less production resources is 100−70=30; including the non-overlapping damage gives 100−(70+40)=−10. This is the net amount in that hypothetical completed scenario, not historical benefit already realized before sale, nor an amount of incurred cost recoverable by refusing to buy now.

If the batch sells for 100, that payment transfers between buyer and seller; it is not another social resource cost. The social account compares assumed realized value, real resource use and third-party damage. Future orders require a separate assessment of avoidable incremental impacts. The figures 100, 70 and 40 and causal attribution are teaching assumptions, not real mine data, and 40 does not represent every ecological value.

module.intro: Separate the resource costs borne by the trading parties from damage borne by third parties outside the transaction, then check whether that outside cost was already included in the original decision.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can the Quoted Price Stay at 100 While 40 Units of Third-Party Damage Still Change the Overall Comparison?
diagramSteps: Assume the already-produced batch is eventually exchanged, realizing buyer value of 100 units at a price also of 100
Record the producer's actual resource cost of 70 and state explicitly that it excludes the third-party damage
Identify the 40 units of uncompensated cleanup damage that the case links causally to the extraction activity and that are borne by a water cooperative outside the transaction
Add production resource cost and third-party damage as 70+40=110, without adding the transaction price of 100 again as another resource cost
For that hypothetical completed scenario, calculate 100−110=−10; current or future decisions need separate avoidable incremental impacts
diagramStepNotes: The 100 is buyer value assumed realized in a completed transaction, not benefit already realized before sale or a claim that all prices equal social value.
The 70 includes labour, equipment, and other resources used by the producer but explicitly excludes the same 40 units of third-party damage.

The 40 can be included this way only because the case assumes evidence has established a causal relationship with the extraction activity; real cases cannot be attributed solely from geographic proximity.
The price of 100 is a transfer from buyer to seller and should not be double-counted as a social resource cost alongside 70 and 40.
The −10 is conditional on realizing 100 in value with no other effects. Incurred costs and future avoidable costs must be separated; this does not determine closure or optimal policy.
mapping: Buyer value 100 → value assumed realized if exchange is completed, not a claim that sale has already occurred.
Producer resource cost of 70 → the resources actually used by the producer to obtain the batch, excluding the third-party 40.
Water cooperative cleanup damage of 40 → an uncompensated external cost borne by a third party outside the transaction.
New line on the procurement sheet → bringing an identified cost that had been outside the buyer-seller accounts back into the decision comparison.
module.boundary: In real cases, water-quality or infrastructure damage may result from natural background conditions, legacy pollution, other facilities, or changes over time, so appropriate source, timing, comparison, and other evidence are needed for case-specific attribution. Mechanisms such as acid mine drainage also depend on minerals, oxygen, water, and site conditions and do not occur at every mine. The values 100, 70, and 40 and their causal relationship are fictional known conditions in this article. They cannot be used to determine responsibility, compensation, optimal tax rates, closure decisions, or the full ecological value of any real mine. An effect that cannot yet be reliably monetized does not therefore have a value of zero.
module.reflection: Suppose the producer pays the cooperative 20 units in compensation, with real resource use and damage otherwise unchanged. Does the 70+40 total in the social account fall by 20? Why?

references.citation: Helbling, T. (2017, May 10). Externalities: Prices Do Not Capture All Costs. Finance & Development, International Monetary Fund.
references.use: Supports that production or consumption can impose effects on third parties outside a transaction that are not fully reflected in prices, and supports distinguishing private costs from social costs. The values 100, 70, and 40 in this article are fictional teaching values and do not come from the IMF source.

references.citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water. (1997). EPA’s National Hardrock Mining Framework, Appendix B, pp. B-3–B-5.
references.use: Supports that acid mine drainage and pollutant release depend on minerals, oxygen, water, and site-specific conditions and can affect surface water and groundwater. This article uses the source only for mechanism background and does not treat the 1997 framework as current regulation, site-specific pollution attribution, or proof of inevitable causation.
