articles.summaryZh: 扫描车的夜班任务原本已经排好，顾川准备签字时，新地质记录送到了桌上。挪一个停放符号很快，重新核清位置却没那么快。
storyParagraphsZh: 夜班开始前，规划室只差把一台无人扫描车的任务表发出去。原计划是让它完成一段数据采集后，停在离第二天第二段扫描最近的位置，这样早班接手时不用多绕路，完整数据包也能赶在上午交给建模同事。顾川正准备签下任务表，地质组在交班前送来一页刚整理完成的新记录。
新记录在原计划区域附近标出一条弱带，具体位置和巷道结构之间的关系还没有核清。顾川把透明图层压上任务图：如果局部岩体脱落影响到车的路线或停放处，设备可能受损，采集工作也可能中断。但这条记录尚不能说明会发生何种失稳、可能性多大。原来安排扫描和停放的区域，正是需要重新核查的地方。
负责排程的同事指着另一个候选停放点：“要不要先挪到这里，今晚照跑？”顾川没有批准。那个候选位置和改后的路线也还没有经过这次新增信息下的专业核查，把图上的设备符号挪过去并不能证明实物已经处在更低风险的位置。他把受影响的夜间扫描段从任务单上暂时划掉，让设备继续留在原有已安排的等待位置，等地质和岩土专业人员先核对位置、结构和作业条件。
受影响任务一划掉，早班就拿不到那段原定数据，建模同事只能先处理已经完成的资料。顾川取消上午交齐完整数据包的安排，等核查结果出来再排新的交付时间。他把候选路线和停放点保留在图上，只标待核查，没有让无人车当晚沿它们去试。
夜班单重新打印时，受影响的扫描段已经移到待办栏。顾川把新地质记录钉在任务图右上角，给建模同事发去数据延期消息。候选路线仍留在待核查栏，这一段没有出现在今晚发出的任务单上。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用地下矿山的纸面任务规划说明岩土工程风险的一个入口：地层或岩体危险信息本身不等于风险结论，风险还与人员、设备或设施是否暴露在所考虑位置，以及潜在后果有关。新的地质证据可以改变原有认识；在信息不足时暂停受影响任务，是对不确定性的管理，并不是宣布危险必然发生或某个替代位置已经安全。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例中的新弱带记录属于危险信息：它提示原计划区域的地层或结构认识需要更新，但单独一条记录不能证明一定会发生局部地层坠落。原计划若执行，会把无人设备带入正在重新评价的位置，因此设备的计划暴露与潜在后果需要和危险信息一起考虑。
本轮实际决策不是把设备从一个已证实危险点移动到一个已证实安全点，而是暂缓受影响任务，让设备不进入尚待核查的计划区域，同时把候选位置和路线保留给专业人员进一步评价。纸上移动符号、没有发生事故或等待一晚，都不能证明危险已经消失。

moduleZh.intro: 当新地质证据改变对计划位置的认识时，先分开看潜在危险、计划暴露对象和可能后果，再决定是否需要暂缓任务等待专业核查。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么一条弱带新记录不足以预言坠落，却仍可能让夜班任务暂缓
diagramSteps: 原计划让无人扫描车完成夜间扫描并进入靠近下一任务的停放区域
交班前新增地质记录提示原计划区域附近存在需要进一步核查的弱带信息
确认新记录尚不能单独证明具体失稳，也不能直接证明另一个候选位置更安全
暂缓受影响扫描任务，让设备不进入尚待核查的计划区域，并把候选路线和位置交专业人员继续评价
记录由此造成的数据与排程延迟，等待位置、结构和工况证据更新后再决定任务
diagramStepNotes: 原位置之所以重要，是因为任务若执行，无人设备会实际进入这次需要重新评价的区域。
弱带线索可能与失稳机制有关，但记录完整性、具体位置关系和现场结构仍需专业评价。
不确定不是‘安全’判定，也不是‘必然失稳’判定；两个相反结论都不能由一条线索直接推出。
本例没有让设备沿未经核查的新路线或候选位置运行，因此不会把纸面方案变化误写成已经改变实际现场暴露。
延期和待核查是管理新证据下不确定性的选择，不是现场进入许可、稳定性计算或专业安全结论。
mapping: 新增弱带记录 → 改变原有地质认识、需要进一步评价的危险线索。
原夜班扫描和停放计划 → 若执行会使无人设备进入所讨论区域的计划暴露。
暂缓受影响任务 → 在新证据未核清前避免执行该计划暴露，而不是宣称危险消失。
完整数据包延期 → 因改变任务安排而产生的具体运营后果。
候选位置标为待核查 → 替代方案仍需证据，不能由纸面移动直接获得安全结论。
moduleZh.boundary: 地下巷道与露天坡体的失稳机制、调查和监测方法并不相同，本篇不把露天坡体方法移植到地下场景，也不给出任何现场阈值、稳定性计算、支护设计或进入许可。弱带、地质结构和其他信息需要由专业人员结合具体位置、工况和更多证据评价。本故事没有人员进入示例危险区，也没有给出真实失稳概率。风险还可能涉及多种事件、暴露和后果；暂停一段任务不表示整个矿山风险为零。
moduleZh.reflection: 假如这一晚没有收到地层坠落报告，能否在新记录与路线关系仍未核清时，直接恢复原扫描段？还缺少什么证据？

referencesZh.citation: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health. (2024, October 9). Mining and Ground Falls. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
referencesZh.use: 支持矿山地层坠落与地质条件、岩体结构和地下开采因素有关，不同地层和结构会影响失稳危险；本篇只借用这一风险背景，不从该页面推导虚构地点的失稳概率、支护要求或现场安全结论。

referencesZh.citation: U.S. Geological Survey. (n.d.). Landslides Glossary.
referencesZh.use: 支持一般风险概念中需要把危险可能性与潜在损失、社会经济后果区分考虑；该来源针对滑坡，本篇只借用危险与后果区分这一一般概念，不将其用于地下巷道的具体参数、监测方法或概率判断。

articles.title: The Gap on the Night-Shift Sheet
articles.summary: The scanner’s night task is already scheduled when a new geological record reaches Gu Chuan’s desk before he signs. Moving a parking symbol is quick; checking what that new position means will take longer.
storyParagraphs: Before the night shift begins, the planning office has only one task sheet left to release for an unmanned scanning unit. The original plan is for it to complete one section of data collection and then park close to the second scanning segment scheduled for the next day. That would let the early shift continue without an extra detour and allow the full data package to reach the modelling team in the morning. Gu Chuan is about to sign the task sheet when the geology team delivers a newly compiled record just before handover.

The new record marks a weak zone near the planned area, but its precise relationship to the underground structure has not been clarified. Gu Chuan overlays the transparent layer on the task map. If a local ground fall reached the vehicle’s route or parking place, the equipment could be damaged and data collection interrupted. The record does not yet establish a failure mechanism or its likelihood. The planned scanning and parking area is exactly where renewed review is needed.

The scheduling colleague points to another candidate parking location. “Why don't we move it here and keep tonight's run?” Gu Chuan does not approve it. That candidate location and the revised route have not yet been professionally reviewed under the newly added information either. Moving the equipment symbol on the map would not prove that the real equipment had been placed in a lower-risk position. He removes the affected night scan segment from the task sheet for the time being, keeps the equipment at its already assigned waiting location, and waits for geological and geotechnical specialists to review the location, structure, and operating conditions first.

With that task removed, the early shift will not receive the planned scan segment, and the modelling team can begin only with data already completed. Gu Chuan cancels the morning commitment for the full package and leaves a new delivery time to be set after review. Candidate routes and parking points stay on the map as pending review; the unit will not be sent along them that night as a test.

When the night-shift sheet is reprinted, the affected scan segment is on the pending list. Gu Chuan pins the new geological record to the upper-right corner of the task map and sends the modelling team a data-delay notice. Candidate routes remain marked for review; this segment is absent from tonight’s issued task sheet.
articles.overall: This article uses an underground-mine planning exercise to introduce one aspect of geotechnical risk: information about a ground or rock-mass hazard is not itself a complete risk conclusion. Risk also depends on whether people, equipment, or facilities would be exposed at the location under consideration and what the potential consequences could be. New geological evidence can change previous understanding; deferring an affected task when information is incomplete is a way of managing uncertainty, not a declaration that failure is inevitable or that an alternative location is already safe.
explanationParagraphs: The new weak-zone record in this example is hazard information: it indicates that understanding of the geology or structure around the originally planned area needs to be updated, but one record alone does not prove that a local ground fall will definitely occur. If the original plan were executed, the unmanned equipment would enter a location now under renewed evaluation, so the planned exposure of the equipment and the possible consequences have to be considered alongside the hazard information.

The actual decision in this round is not to move the equipment from a proven dangerous location to a proven safe one. It is to defer the affected task so that the equipment does not enter the still-unreviewed planned area, while leaving candidate locations and routes for professional assessment. Moving a symbol on paper, having no accident, or waiting overnight cannot prove that the hazard has disappeared.

module.intro: When new geological evidence changes understanding of a planned location, separate the potential hazard, the planned exposed object, and the possible consequence before deciding whether to defer the task pending professional review.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can a New Weak-Zone Record Be Insufficient to Predict a Ground Fall Yet Still Be Enough to Pause the Night Task?
diagramSteps: The original plan sends the unmanned scanner through the night scan and into a parking area close to the next task
Just before handover, a new geological record identifies weak-zone information near the planned area that requires further review
Confirm that the new record alone does not prove a specific failure and does not directly prove that another candidate location is safer
Defer the affected scan task so that the equipment does not enter the unreviewed planned area, and leave candidate routes and locations for professional evaluation
Record the resulting data and scheduling delay, then wait for updated evidence on location, structure, and operating conditions before deciding the task
diagramStepNotes: The original location matters because, if the plan were executed, the unmanned equipment would physically enter the area now requiring renewed evaluation.
Weak-zone information may relate to an instability mechanism, but record completeness, precise positional relationships, and underground structure still require professional assessment.
Uncertainty is neither a finding of 'safe' nor a finding of 'failure is inevitable'; neither opposite conclusion can be drawn directly from one clue.
This example does not send the equipment along an unreviewed new route or into an unreviewed candidate location, so a paper-plan change is not misrepresented as an actual change in field exposure.
Delay and pending review are choices for managing uncertainty under new evidence, not entry authorization, stability calculation, or a professional safety conclusion.
mapping: New weak-zone record → hazard information that changes prior geological understanding and requires further evaluation.
Original night scanning and parking plan → planned exposure that would place the unmanned equipment in the area under discussion if executed.
Deferring the affected task → avoiding execution of the planned exposure while the new evidence remains unresolved, not declaring that the hazard has disappeared.
Delayed full data package → the concrete operational consequence of changing the task plan.
Candidate location marked pending review → an alternative still requiring evidence rather than becoming safe merely because it was moved on paper.
module.boundary: Underground workings and open-pit slopes have different failure mechanisms, investigation methods, and monitoring approaches. This article does not transfer open-slope monitoring methods into an underground setting and does not provide field thresholds, stability calculations, support design, construction guidance, or entry authorization. Weak zones, geological structures, and other evidence require professional evaluation together with the specific location, operating conditions, and additional information. No personnel enter the example hazard area, and no real failure probability is provided. Risk can also involve multiple events, exposures, and consequences; deferring one task does not mean overall mine risk is zero.
module.reflection: Suppose no ground fall is reported that night. Can the original scan segment simply resume while the new record’s relationship to the route remains unresolved? What evidence is still missing?

references.citation: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health. (2024, October 9). Mining and Ground Falls. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
references.use: Supports that mining ground falls are related to geological conditions, rock-mass structure, and underground mining factors, and that different ground and structural conditions affect instability hazards. This article uses only that risk background and does not derive a failure probability, support requirement, or field safety conclusion for the fictional location.

references.citation: U.S. Geological Survey. (n.d.). Landslides Glossary.
references.use: Supports the general risk distinction between hazard likelihood and potential losses or socioeconomic consequences. Because the source concerns landslides, this article borrows only the general distinction between hazard and consequence and does not use it for underground-workings parameters, monitoring methods, or probability judgments.

articles.summaryZh: 阅读节明天开场，花箱和桌椅都已摆好。周宁准备签字收工时，却在入口前遇见一辆过不去的婴儿车。
storyParagraphsZh: 周末阅读节第二天就要开场，周宁负责图书馆外那段小街的最后布置。花箱、展板、阅读桌和咖啡摊都已经照图摆好，工作人员正等她签字收工。她从公交站方向走过来，却在离入口不远的地方停了下来：一辆双人婴儿车和拖着书箱的工作人员刚好迎面相遇，两边都停了下来，工作人员得先把书箱拉回一点，婴儿车才能通过。
周宁没有只站在原地看，而是自己继续往入口走。前面有人站着等朋友，后面的人便从花箱旁绕过；长椅上的老人想看入口，视线却被一块展板挡住；工作人员推着装书的小车转弯时，又得先等咖啡桌边的人让开。每一处单独看都还能使用，可这些动作连续发生时，这段本来不长的路不断要求人停、绕、让。
入口两边那两只大花箱是周宁最不想动的。它们在布置图上正好把门框住，咖啡摊主也已经按旁边的空位准备多展开一张桌子。周宁在长椅上坐了一会儿，看见另一个推婴儿车的人走近入口，又在等候的人身后拐了一次。她站起来，让布置组移开一只花箱，把高展板贴近墙边，再把等候的位置从主要通路上让开。
咖啡摊主问备用桌怎么办。周宁看了看刚腾出的路线，最后还是摇头：“这张先别开。”少一张桌，意味着少一个售卖位置；另一只花箱也被移到较远的墙边，原来入口两侧完全对称的布置没有了。可工作人员再推书箱经过时，不必先等入口的人全部散开，长椅前也留出了完整的停留空间。
第二天开场，一个孩子从公交站方向跑到入口前，又停下来等身后的家长。家长推着车走到他旁边时，另一位抱着书的人仍能从旁边通过。周宁站在长椅边，看见等人的、坐着的和继续往前走的人同时留在这一小段街上。那只花箱靠墙摆着。推车的人经过时，不再需要往它旁边绕。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一段从公交站到图书馆入口的具体使用经历说明人性尺度的一个入口：空间是否好用，不只看平面是否整齐或设施是否靠得近，还要看人在地面如何看见、通过、等待、休息和与他人错身。尺度和细节需要回应不同身体、速度和公共空间活动。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例中，花箱、展板、座椅和售卖桌本身都不是问题；问题出现在它们与真实身体移动、视线、停留和等待叠加之后。周宁沿明确的公交站—入口路线观察这些动作，再调整设施位置，说明人性尺度关注的是人与空间之间的实际关系，而不是单纯把建筑或设施做得更小。
结尾只展示开场时几种具体使用动作能够同时发生，并不能证明所有年龄、身体条件、时段或活动都已经得到验证。真实可用性还需要在不同时间、不同使用者和具体当地标准下继续观察和判断；本故事不提供通用尺寸、无障碍合规结论或现场设计标准。

moduleZh.intro: 从一条明确的步行路线出发，观察人在地面如何通过、停留、看见和彼此避让，再判断设施位置是否支持这些真实动作。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么看起来整齐的入口，在地面上仍可能不断让人停、绕、让
diagramSteps: 从公交站方向沿实际路线走向图书馆入口，而不是只看布置图
观察婴儿车、运书小车、等候者和坐下者如何共享同一段空间
发现花箱、展板和售卖桌在连续动作中造成绕行、视线遮挡和相互等待
先后移开入口两只花箱，调整展板和等候位置，并不再展开备用售卖桌
在开场后的具体场景中观察通过、停留和等待是否能够同时发生
diagramStepNotes: 明确起点和终点能让判断落在实际使用任务上，而不是抽象评价空间是否漂亮。
不同身体、速度和活动方式会占用空间、改变视线和停留方式，不能只按一个平均使用者判断。
设施更近或数量更多并不自动改善体验，位置不当反而可能增加绕行和冲突。
调整空间会有代价，本例中少一个售卖位置并失去原来的对称入口构图。
一次观察只能说明当时这些具体动作的表现，不能推出所有人和所有时段都同样可用。
mapping: 公交站到图书馆入口 → 明确的实际使用路线。
婴儿车、书箱小车和等候者 → 不同身体占用、移动速度和停留需求。
被挪开的花箱与备用桌 → 为连续通过和停留让出的空间与经营代价。
长椅前恢复的视线和空间 → 人的感知、停留与街道边缘关系。
开场时同时发生的走、等、坐 → 地面使用体验的具体观察，而非全面可用性证明。
moduleZh.boundary: 人性尺度不是“小建筑”的同义词，也不是只缩短距离或按单一平均身体设计。空间还要面对不同年龄、行动能力、视觉感知、移动速度和公共活动。整齐、美观、设施更近或行人变多，都不能单独证明空间对所有人可用。本例只说明一个虚构阅读节入口在特定时段的具体观察，不提供通用尺寸、现实合规判断或完整专业设计。
moduleZh.reflection: 假如入口变宽了，一位看不清展板的读者仍找不到门，你还会观察哪些具体使用动作，才知道这次布置照顾到了谁、遗漏了谁？

referencesZh.use: 支持从人的视高、身体使用、街道边缘、设施位置和无障碍活动理解空间，并通过不同时间的实际使用观察设计效果；本篇借用这些设计原则，不把它们当作全球统一尺寸标准，也不把虚构现场观察当成来源实测数据。

referencesZh.use: 支持连续无阻的步行路线、停留和休息，并强调考虑不同年龄、感知和行动能力；本篇不采用来源中的速度或尺寸作为通用阈值，也不由一次观察推出所有使用者都已得到满足。

articles.title: The Two Planters by the Entrance
articles.summary: The reading festival opens tomorrow, and the planters and tables are already in place. Zhou Ning is about to sign off on the setup when a stroller gets stuck near the entrance.
storyParagraphs: The weekend reading festival opens the next day, and Zhou Ning is responsible for the final setup of the small street outside the library. The planters, display boards, reading tables, and coffee stall have all been placed according to the plan, and the staff are waiting for her sign-off before leaving. As she walks in from the bus-stop direction, she stops not far from the entrance: a double stroller and a staff member pulling a box of books meet head-on. Both stop. The staff member has to pull the box back a little before the stroller can pass.

Zhou Ning does not simply stand there and look. She continues walking toward the entrance herself. Someone ahead is waiting for a friend, so people behind detour around a planter; an older person sitting on the bench wants to see the entrance, but a display board blocks the view; when a staff member turns with a cart of books, they have to wait for people beside the coffee table to move. Each spot can still be used on its own, but when these actions occur one after another, this short stretch keeps making people stop, detour, and give way.

The two large planters on either side of the entrance are the elements Zhou Ning least wants to move. On the setup drawing, they frame the doorway perfectly, and the coffee vendor has already prepared to open an extra table in the space beside them. Zhou Ning sits on the bench for a while and sees another person pushing a stroller approach the entrance, then make another turn behind the people waiting there. She stands up and asks the setup team to move one planter, place the tall display board closer to the wall, and shift the waiting area out of the main path.

The coffee vendor asks what to do with the spare table. Zhou Ning looks at the route they have just opened up and finally shakes her head. “Don't set this one up.” One fewer table means one fewer sales position. The other planter is also moved farther toward the wall, and the entrance is no longer perfectly symmetrical. But when staff push the book cart through again, they no longer have to wait for everyone near the entrance to clear, and the space in front of the bench remains open for stopping.

When the event opens the next day, a child runs from the bus-stop direction to the entrance and then stops to wait for the parent behind. As the parent reaches the child with a stroller, another person carrying books can still pass beside them. Zhou Ning stands near the bench and sees people waiting, sitting, and continuing forward at the same time on this small stretch of street. The planter stands against the wall. People pushing strollers no longer have to detour around it.
articles.overall: This article uses a specific journey from a bus stop to a library entrance to introduce one aspect of human scale: whether a space works well depends not only on whether its plan looks orderly or whether facilities are close together, but also on how people at ground level see, pass, wait, rest, and move around one another. Scale and detail need to respond to different bodies, speeds, and public-space activities.
explanationParagraphs: In this example, the planters, display boards, seating, and sales table are not problems by themselves. The problem emerges when their positions interact with real bodily movement, sightlines, stopping, and waiting. Zhou Ning observes these activities along a defined bus-stop-to-entrance route and then changes the placement of facilities, showing that human scale concerns the actual relationship between people and space rather than simply making buildings or facilities smaller.

The ending shows only that several specific activities can occur together during the opening period. It does not prove that every age group, physical condition, time period, or activity has been fully accommodated. Real usability still requires observation and assessment across different users, times, and applicable local standards. This story provides no universal dimensions, accessibility-compliance conclusion, or site-design standard.

module.intro: Start with a defined walking route, observe how people at ground level pass, stop, see, and move around one another, and then judge whether the placement of facilities supports those real activities.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can an Entrance That Looks Orderly Still Keep Making People Stop, Detour, and Give Way at Ground Level?
diagramSteps: Walk from the bus-stop direction toward the library entrance along the actual route rather than judging only from the layout drawing
Observe how a stroller, a book cart, people waiting, and people sitting share the same stretch of space
Notice that planters, a display board, and a sales table create detours, blocked sightlines, and mutual waiting when activities occur in sequence
Move both entrance planters in turn, adjust the display board and waiting area, and leave the spare sales table folded
During the opening period, observe whether passing, stopping, and waiting can occur at the same time in the specific scene
diagramStepNotes: A clear origin and destination keep the judgment tied to an actual use task rather than an abstract opinion about whether the space looks attractive.
Different bodies, movement speeds, and activities occupy space and change sightlines and stopping patterns, so one average user cannot represent everyone.
Closer facilities or more facilities do not automatically improve experience; poor placement can instead increase detours and conflicts.
Changing the space has a cost: this example loses one sales position and the original symmetrical entrance composition.
One observation can show only how these specific activities perform at that time; it cannot establish equal usability for everyone or at all times.
mapping: Bus stop to library entrance → the defined real-use route.
Stroller, book cart, and people waiting → different bodily footprints, movement speeds, and stopping needs.
Moved planter and spare table → space and commercial capacity given up to support continuous passage and stopping.
Restored sightline and space in front of the bench → the relationship between human perception, staying, and the street edge.
Walking, waiting, and sitting happening together during opening → a concrete observation of ground-level use rather than proof of universal usability.
module.boundary: Human scale is not a synonym for 'small buildings,' nor does it mean simply shortening distances or designing for one average body. Space must also respond to different ages, mobility abilities, visual perception, movement speeds, and public activities. Orderliness, visual appeal, closer facilities, or more pedestrians cannot by themselves prove that a space works for everyone. This example describes only a fictional reading-festival entrance during a particular period and does not provide universal dimensions, real-world compliance judgments, or a complete professional design.
module.reflection: Suppose the entrance is wider, but a reader who cannot see the display board still cannot find the door. What would you observe to learn whom the layout serves and whom it misses?

references.use: Supports understanding space through human eye level, bodily use, street edges, facility placement, and accessible activity, and through observation of actual use at different times. This article borrows those design principles without treating them as universal dimensional standards or presenting the fictional observations as source measurements.

articles.summaryZh: 托育点、眼镜店和面包店都在家门口，陈禾却接连两天没能办完下班后的几件事。他带去观察会的，是一条绕了又绕的路线。
storyParagraphsZh: 陈禾下班后通常只有四十来分钟处理家里的杂事。那天他要从街区里的托育点接女儿、取已经修好的眼镜，再买第二天早餐。搬来这里时，他最看中的就是住宅楼下和内街周边已经有这些日常用途，不必为了三件小事分别去三个相距很远的地方。可第一次真把它们串在一起，他还是没能一次办完。
托育点就在住宅内街一侧，接到女儿后几步就能看到面包店的窗户，眼镜店也在同一街区。可眼镜店面向内街的侧门一直锁着，顾客只能绕到外侧入口。那天陈禾抱着女儿绕过去时，眼镜店已经关门；再回到面包店，卷帘门也落下了。第二天他接到女儿后先买了面包，才去绕那段路，仍然错过了眼镜店的取件时段。修好的眼镜一直留在店里。
开业后的使用观察会上，陈禾把自己的路线画在纸上。他从托育点出发，先指了指能直接看到的面包店，再把笔绕到眼镜店外侧入口，最后才回到住宅门厅：“这几件事我都要办，可这一圈还是被门和时间拆开了。”运营人员跟着他把这趟路重新走了一遍，没有再讨论要不要新增第四家店，而是开始看现有几个地方之间到底哪里接不上。
后来眼镜店开放了面向内街的侧门，面包店把部分晚间营业时间向后挪，托育点到住宅内街的步行通道保持开放。为了不让新的步行高峰和送货撞在一起，物业又调整了部分货运安排。商户要重新排班，物业也得把新的送货时段逐一通知商家。陈禾来接女儿的那段时间，内街入口留给步行的人。
几天后，陈禾接到女儿后没有再走出街区。他们沿内街先取了眼镜，又在面包店关门前买到早餐，最后直接走回住宅门厅。女儿一手拿着眼镜盒，一手抱着纸袋，问他：“今天还要去哪儿？”陈禾按下电梯键：“没有了，今天这三件事就在回家的路上。”
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一位家长的一趟下班行程说明混合功能开发的一个入口：当住宅、照护、零售和生活服务等相容用途位于同一街区并且实际连通时，原本分散的日常任务可能被组合成一趟更直接的行程。但用途邻近只是基础，入口、开放时间、通道和运营协调仍会决定实际可达性。
explanationParagraphsZh: 故事中的便利变化不是单靠延长面包店营业时间产生的。住宅、托育、眼镜服务和零售原本已经在同一生活圈内，这使陈禾有可能在一次下班步行中串联多种日常任务；侧门开放、通道保持可用和时间协调则让这些已经相邻的用途真正连接起来。
混合功能不等于把所有用途都挤在一起，也不保证任何街区天然便利。货运、噪声、排放、营业时间、住宅负担和不同使用者需求都可能产生冲突。本例只说明陈禾这一趟具体行程如何变化，不能据此推出整个街区租金更低、更公平、通勤更短或交通效果都由用途混合单独造成。

moduleZh.intro: 先看一趟真实生活行程需要哪些日常用途，再检查这些用途是否既相邻又在时间和入口上真正连得起来。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么几个地方都在同一个街区，陈禾第一次仍然办不完三件事
diagramSteps: 陈禾下班后需要接孩子、取眼镜并购买第二天早餐
住宅、托育点、眼镜店和面包店已经位于同一个街区，为一趟步行行程提供多个相邻节点
眼镜店侧门关闭、营业时间不匹配，使这些近距离用途仍被实际路线拆开
运营方调整侧门、部分营业时段和步行通道，同时重新协调货运
调整后陈禾能在同一趟回家步行中完成三件事，但商户和物业承担新的运营协调成本
diagramStepNotes: 故事的起点是一个具体生活任务，而不是抽象评价街区功能数量。
不同用途的相容邻近提供了组合行程的基础；如果这些功能原本相距很远，单独调整一扇门不会产生相同结果。
直线距离近不代表实际可达，入口方向、开门时间和通道状态都可能改变真实行程。
货运与居民步行可能冲突，因此混合功能仍需要运营和空间协调。
这一趟行程改善不能外推为所有居民、所有时段或所有城市交通结果都相同。
mapping: 托育点 → 日常照护用途。
眼镜店 → 生活服务用途。
面包店 → 日常零售用途。
住宅门厅 → 行程结束的居住用途。
侧门、通道和营业时间 → 把用途邻近转化为实际可达性的连接条件。
moduleZh.boundary: 混合功能开发强调在一栋楼、街区或邻近区域组合相容的住宅、工作、商业和公共服务等用途，但不是用途越多越好，也不是把冲突用途全部挤在一起。实际效果还受入口、营业时间、步行网络、交通方式、货运、噪声、排放和运营安排影响。用途混合本身不保证低租金、公平、短通勤或便利，也不能把一次具体行程改善全部归因于单一规划因素。
moduleZh.reflection: 假如托育点搬到必须乘车才能到的另一个街区，只延长面包店营业时间，还能让这三件事成为同一趟步行吗？为什么？

referencesZh.citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. (n.d.). About Smart Growth.
referencesZh.use: 支持相容用途混合、步行街坊、住房选择和多种交通方式作为综合智慧增长策略，并支持紧凑混合用途与交通选择结合时有助于日常出行便利；本篇只借用这一概念关系，不把一次虚构行程改善视为用途混合单独造成的普遍效果，也不推导租金、噪声或通勤必然下降。

articles.title: Three Errands on the Way Home
articles.summary: The childcare centre, optical shop and bakery are all close to home, yet Chen He fails to finish his errands two evenings in a row. He brings the neighbourhood meeting a route full of detours.
storyParagraphs: After work, Chen He usually has only around forty minutes to deal with household errands. That day he needs to pick up his daughter from the childcare centre in the neighbourhood, collect his repaired glasses, and buy breakfast for the next morning. When he moved there, one of the things he valued most was that these daily uses were already around the residential building and the internal street, so he would not have to travel to three far-apart places for three small tasks. But the first time he actually tries to combine them, he still cannot finish everything in one trip.

The childcare centre is on one side of the residential internal street. After collecting his daughter, he can see the bakery window just a few steps away, and the optical shop is in the same neighbourhood. But the shop's side door facing the internal street stays locked, so customers must go around to the outer entrance. By the time Chen He carries his daughter around that day, the optical shop is closed; when they return to the bakery, its shutter is down too. The next day, he collects his daughter and buys bread first, then takes the detour, but still misses the optical shop's collection window. The repaired glasses remain in the shop.

At a post-opening use-observation meeting, Chen He draws his route on paper. Starting from the childcare centre, he points first to the bakery that is directly visible, then traces the pen around to the optical shop's outer entrance, and only after that returns to the residential lobby. “These are all errands I need to finish, but this one trip still gets broken apart by doors and timing.” The operators walk the route with him. Instead of discussing whether to add a fourth shop, they start looking at where the existing places fail to connect.

Later, the optical shop opens its side door onto the internal street, the bakery shifts part of its evening opening period later, and the walking connection from the childcare centre to the residential internal street remains open. To avoid a new pedestrian peak colliding with deliveries, the property manager also adjusts part of the delivery schedule. Shops have to rearrange staffing, and the property manager must notify each business of the new delivery times. During the period when Chen He picks up his daughter, the internal-street entrance is kept clear for people on foot.

A few days later, Chen He picks up his daughter and does not leave the neighbourhood again. They walk along the internal street, collect the glasses first, buy breakfast before the bakery closes, and then go straight back to the residential lobby. His daughter holds the glasses case in one hand and the paper bag in the other. “Do we still have to go anywhere?” she asks. Chen He presses the lift button. “No. Today those three things were all on the way home.”
articles.overall: This article uses one parent's after-work trip to introduce one aspect of mixed-use development: when compatible uses such as housing, childcare, retail, and daily services are located in the same neighbourhood and are effectively connected, tasks that would otherwise be dispersed may be combined into a more direct trip. But proximity is only the foundation; entrances, opening hours, routes, and operating coordination still determine actual accessibility.
explanationParagraphs: The improvement in this story is not produced simply by extending the bakery's opening hours. Housing, childcare, optical services, and retail were already located within the same everyday activity area, making it possible for Chen He to combine several daily tasks into one after-work walking trip. Opening the side door, keeping the route available, and coordinating operating times then allow those already-nearby uses to function as an actual connected journey.

Mixed use does not mean placing every possible use together, nor does it guarantee that any neighbourhood will automatically be convenient. Freight activity, noise, emissions, opening hours, residential burdens, and the needs of different users can all create conflicts. This example only shows how Chen He's particular trip changes; it cannot establish that the whole neighbourhood has lower rents, greater fairness, shorter commutes, or transport effects caused by mixed use alone.

articles.summaryZh: 合作社想在旧印刷厂开学习厨房和手作课。许棠舍不得那排旧长桌，可把新课表放进旧房间，并不像换块招牌那么简单。
storyParagraphsZh: 街区合作社租下了一座停用多年的小印刷厂，准备把它变成长期开放的社区学习厨房和手作教室。许棠第一次进去，就喜欢上中央的大开间、高窗和一排结实的旧长桌；那些桌子很适合画图、装配和手作课程。真正让方案卡住的是后部：旧的小房间和内部隔墙把未来需要的厨房工作区、清洗、储物和通行路线切得七零八落。
有人主张尽量一处都别动，也有人觉得既然要改用途，不如把内部全部清空。合作社没有靠肉眼决定哪些能留，而是先请专业团队针对新用途完成调查。调查结论认为中央开间、高窗和部分旧构件可以继续利用；同时确认几处非承重内部隔墙可以按新用途调整，厨房服务、清洗和其他技术设施则需要重新布置和接入。
方案讨论时，团队用平面模型和流程卡做了一次施工前演练。许棠把标着手作课的卡片放到旧长桌对应的位置，把厨房课程卡片放到计划新增的独立食物处理区；旧长桌只安排手作，不作食物接触台面。她沿图上的路线移动两组流程卡，卡片走到后部时，取物、清洗和返回的路线都挤在原有小房间的转折处。
许棠把模型里那一段经专业调查确认可以调整的非承重内部隔墙拿掉，重新留出服务和通行位置。这个选择让项目不再是‘刷墙、搬机器、换招牌’那么简单：改造预算增加，开放日期后移，旧长桌还要修整，新的厨房工作区、清洗、储物和设备服务也要按方案施工。但她没有因此放弃那些真正帮助新用途的旧空间。
改造完成并投入使用后，手作课仍围着修整后的旧长桌开始，厨房课程则在独立的新工作区准备食材。下课后，两组学员从重新组织过的后部空间分别去收工具和清洗，没有再堵在原来的转折处。许棠最后关灯时，高窗和旧厂编号还在，原来那段非承重内部隔墙的位置已经改变。她收好第二天的课表，放在一张旧长桌上。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用旧印刷厂改为社区学习厨房和手作教室的故事说明适应性再利用的一个入口：旧建筑中的有用实体和重要特征可以继续发挥价值，但新的长期用途往往也需要真实改变内部安排、技术服务和运行方式。关键不是一律保留或一律拆除，而是依据调查选择哪些值得保留、哪些必须改变。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例把技术可行性作为虚构专业调查结论，而不是由许棠凭肉眼判断。调查确认中央开间、高窗和部分旧构件可以继续使用，也确认几处非承重内部隔墙能够按新用途调整；施工前的模型与流程演练只用于检查新用途的空间关系，并不等于未经改造的旧厂已经可以开展厨房活动。
适应性再利用不仅是换招牌、保留外皮或临时借用旧空间，也不要求所有旧部分原样留下。新用途还需要满足安全、可达性、技术服务和持续经营等实际条件。保留旧建筑也不自动意味着项目一定更便宜或全生命周期影响更低，这些结果需要另外调查和比较。

moduleZh.intro: 先确认旧建筑哪些实体和特征对新用途仍有价值，再依据专业调查识别必须改变的内部安排和服务条件。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么旧印刷厂既保留长桌和高窗，又必须改变部分内部隔墙
diagramSteps: 确定新用途是长期运行的社区学习厨房和手作教室，而不是一次临时活动
由专业调查确认中央开间、高窗和部分旧构件可以继续利用
同一调查确认几处非承重内部隔墙可调整，新厨房、清洗、储物和技术服务需要重新安排
在施工前用模型和流程卡检查两类课程的取物、清洗和通行关系，并据此调整方案
施工完成后让保留空间和新增设施共同支持新的长期日常使用
diagramStepNotes: 长期用途转换要求考虑持续运行，而不仅是一次活动能否临时塞进旧空间。
可保留部分来自专业调查的虚构结论，不代表所有旧建筑中的类似构件都适合继续使用。
只有经专业调查确认的非承重内部隔墙才进入本故事的调整范围，不涉及现实结构许可判断。
模型演练发生在施工前，厨房食物处理只存在于计划中的独立新工作区，不在旧长桌上实际进行。
改造完成后是否长期可行还涉及运营、维护和其他条件，本故事只展示一个有限入口。
mapping: 中央大开间与高窗 → 旧建筑中继续帮助新用途的空间特征。
旧长桌 → 经修整后继续服务非食物接触手作活动的旧构件。
非承重内部隔墙调整 → 为新用途真实改变旧安排的一处具体改造。
独立新厨房工作区 → 新用途需要新增而不能由旧设施直接替代的功能。
预算增加和延期 → 选择性保留与真实改造带来的项目代价。
moduleZh.boundary: 适应性再利用不是只换招牌、只保留外皮、完全不动或一律拆除。具体旧建筑是否适合新用途，需要专业调查其结构、可达性、机电服务、技术条件和长期管理。本篇只把若干非承重内部隔墙可调整作为虚构专业结论，不提供现实拆改许可、结构安全判断或施工指导。保留建筑也不自动证明项目比新建更便宜、更低碳或更适合，环境与经济结果需要单独比较。
moduleZh.reflection: 假如旧厂房只借给手作班办一天活动，结束后仍恢复空置，这与故事中的长期改用有什么不同？你还需要知道哪些条件？

referencesZh.citation: Historic England. (2024, August 14). Heritage Works for Housing.
referencesZh.use: 支持为旧建筑寻找可持续的新用途，并强调技术调查、长期使用和管理的重要性；本篇借用这些一般再利用原则，不把住宅语境资料当作虚构印刷厂的结构合格证明或现实许可依据。

referencesZh.citation: Historic England. (n.d.). Heritage Works for Housing: Managing Change.
referencesZh.use: 支持由技术团队综合考虑新用途需要的改变、机电服务和既有建筑价值，并提醒隐含与运行影响需要一起考虑；本篇不把英国历史建筑指导当作其他地区法规，也不据此声称保留建筑必然比新建更便宜或更低碳。

articles.title: A New Timetable for the Old Printing Works
articles.summary: A cooperative wants to open a teaching kitchen and craft classroom in an old printing works. Xu Tang wants to keep the old worktables, but fitting the new timetable into the old rooms takes more than a new sign.
storyParagraphs: A neighbourhood cooperative rents a small printing works that has been unused for years and plans to turn it into a community teaching kitchen and craft classroom for long-term use. On her first visit, Xu Tang immediately likes the large central room, the high windows, and a row of sturdy old worktables; those tables would suit drawing, assembly, and craft classes. What stalls the plan is the rear of the building: the old small rooms and interior partitions break up the future kitchen work area, washing, storage, and circulation routes.

Some people argue that almost nothing should be changed, while others say that if the use is changing anyway, the entire interior should simply be cleared out. The cooperative does not decide by eye what can stay. It first commissions a professional team to investigate the building for the proposed new use. The survey concludes that the central room, high windows, and some existing components can continue to be used. It also confirms that several non-load-bearing interior partitions can be adjusted for the new use, while kitchen services, washing facilities, and other technical systems need to be rearranged and newly connected.

During design discussions, the team runs a pre-construction exercise with a floor-plan model and process cards. Xu Tang places the craft-class cards at the positions of the old worktables and the kitchen-class cards in the planned separate new food-preparation area. The old tables are assigned only to crafts, not food contact. She moves the two sets of cards along the routes on the plan. At the rear rooms, the routes for collecting items, washing, and returning all converge at the turns between the old small rooms.

Xu Tang removes from the model the section of non-load-bearing interior partition that the professional survey has confirmed can be altered and redraws the service and circulation space. The choice means the project is no longer as simple as 'paint the walls, move the machines, and change the sign.' The renovation budget rises, the opening date moves back, the old worktables still need refurbishment, and the new kitchen work area, washing, storage, and equipment services all have to be built according to the plan. But she does not give up the old spaces that genuinely help the new use.

After the renovation is completed and the building enters use, craft classes still begin around the refurbished old worktables, while kitchen classes prepare food in the separate new work area. After class, the two groups move through the reorganized rear space to put away tools and use the washing facilities without bunching up at the old turn. When Xu Tang switches off the lights at the end of the day, the high windows and old factory number are still there, while the position of the former non-load-bearing interior partition has changed. She puts away the next day's timetable on one of the old worktables.
articles.overall: This article uses the conversion of an old printing works into a community teaching kitchen and craft classroom to introduce one aspect of adaptive reuse: useful physical fabric and important features of an existing building can continue to provide value, while a new long-term use may still require real changes to internal arrangements, technical services, and operating patterns. The key is not to preserve everything or remove everything, but to investigate which parts are worth retaining and which need to change.
explanationParagraphs: This example treats technical feasibility as the conclusion of a fictional professional survey rather than something Xu Tang determines by visual inspection. The survey confirms that the central room, high windows, and some existing components can continue in use, and that several non-load-bearing interior partitions can be adjusted for the new use. The pre-construction model and process exercise is used only to test spatial relationships for the proposed functions; it does not mean that kitchen activities can already take place in the unmodified old building.

Adaptive reuse is more than changing a sign, retaining only a façade, or temporarily borrowing an old space, and it does not require every old element to remain untouched. The new use still has to meet real conditions for safety, accessibility, technical services, and continuing operation. Retaining an existing building also does not automatically mean that a project will be cheaper or have lower whole-life impacts; those outcomes require separate investigation and comparison.

module.intro: First identify which physical elements and features of the existing building still provide value for the new use, then use professional investigation to identify which internal arrangements and service conditions must change.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can the Old Printing Works Keep Its Long Tables and High Windows Yet Still Need Some Interior Partitions to Change?
diagramSteps: Define the new use as a long-term community teaching kitchen and craft classroom rather than a one-off temporary activity
Use professional investigation to confirm that the central open room, high windows, and some existing components can continue to be used
Use the same investigation to confirm that several non-load-bearing interior partitions can be adjusted and that new kitchen, washing, storage, and technical services need to be reorganized
Before construction, use a floor-plan model and process cards to examine how the two types of classes would collect items, wash, and circulate, and revise the design accordingly
After construction, let the retained spaces and new facilities work together to support the building's new long-term daily use
diagramStepNotes: Long-term change of use requires consideration of continued operation rather than only whether one temporary event can fit inside the old space.
The elements identified for retention come from the fictional professional survey and do not imply that similar elements in every old building are suitable for continued use.
Only the non-load-bearing interior partitions confirmed by the professional survey are within the alteration scope of this story; it makes no real-world structural-permission judgment.
The model exercise takes place before construction. Food preparation exists only in the planned separate new kitchen area and is not actually performed on the old worktables.
Long-term viability after renovation also depends on operation, maintenance, and other conditions; this story shows only one limited entry point.
mapping: Large central room and high windows → existing spatial features that continue to help the new use.
Old worktables → existing components refurbished for non-food-contact craft activities.
Adjustment of non-load-bearing interior partitions → one specific physical alteration required by the new use.
Separate new kitchen work area → a new function that cannot simply be substituted by the old facilities.
Higher budget and delayed opening → the project cost of selective retention combined with real alteration.
module.boundary: Adaptive reuse is not merely changing a sign, retaining only the exterior, leaving everything untouched, or demolishing everything. Whether a specific old building is suitable for a new use requires professional investigation of structure, accessibility, mechanical and electrical services, technical conditions, and long-term management. This article treats the adjustability of several non-load-bearing interior partitions only as a fictional professional conclusion and provides no real demolition permission, structural-safety judgment, or construction guidance. Retaining a building also does not automatically prove that the project is cheaper, lower-carbon, or more suitable than new construction; environmental and economic outcomes require separate comparison.
module.reflection: If the old printing works hosted a craft class for one day and then stood empty again, how would that differ from the lasting change of use in the story? What else would you need to know?

references.citation: Historic England. (2024, August 14). Heritage Works for Housing.
references.use: Supports finding sustainable new uses for existing buildings and emphasizes the importance of technical investigation, long-term use, and management. This article borrows those general reuse principles without treating the housing-context guidance as structural approval or a real permitting basis for the fictional printing works.

references.citation: Historic England. (n.d.). Heritage Works for Housing: Managing Change.
references.use: Supports technical teams considering together the changes required by a new use, mechanical and electrical services, and the value of an existing building, while also considering embodied and operational impacts. This article does not treat UK historic-building guidance as regulation for other jurisdictions and does not use it to claim that retaining a building is necessarily cheaper or lower-carbon than new construction.

articles.summaryZh: 三枚硬币一放，平台模型的一角就沉了下去。顾言望着旁边那根粗柱，不明白它为什么一点也没帮上忙。
storyParagraphsZh: 社区建筑展要摆一座巴掌大的平台模型，参观者可以把三枚硬币叠在平台角上的黄色圆点处，看模型怎样把重量传到底下。顾言第一次按这个摆法试演时，平台一角往下沉，三枚硬币随着斜面滑到桌上。最奇怪的是，下沉位置旁边明明立着一根比其他柱子还粗的小柱。
顾言把模型举起来看底面。横梁托着面板，端部却只从粗柱柱顶旁边经过，并没有真正落上去。两个部件靠得很近，中间仍有一条空隙。他没有换一根更粗的柱子，而是去找能放进这个位置的小托座。
那块透明说明牌恰好挡着梁端与柱顶之间的位置，顾言先把它移到模型外侧，才放进小托座。原来的面板、横梁、柱子、底座和其他支承都保留。他把同样三枚硬币按原叠法放回黄色圆点，平台这次保持住了。他顺着新增支路看过去：面板压着横梁，横梁经过托座压到立柱，立柱再把一部分重量传到底座和桌面。
顾言取走硬币，拆下托座，再按相同位置和叠法放回三枚，平台角又往下沉。他再次取走硬币，把托座装回。移到外面的说明牌让展示台显得零碎了些，他仍把它留在那里，让托座完整地露出来。
展览开始后，一位参观者拿起那三枚演示硬币，照黄色圆点重新叠好。平台没有再往下歪。她弯腰看见横梁下面露出的托座，先指了指它，又指向底座：“这里真的接上以后，才有路走下去？”顾言把模型轻轻转向她：“对，这一条现在接上了。”三枚硬币还停在圆点上。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用低风险桌面重力模型说明荷载路径的一个入口：荷载需要通过实际构件以及方向合适的接触或连接，连续传到支承和最终基础。附近存在强构件并不足够，如果中间缺少真实传力环节，那根构件就不会自动加入所讨论的荷载路径。
explanationParagraphsZh: 向下的重力荷载可以沿面板、横梁、实际承压支承、立柱和底座逐步传递。判断路径时要逐段问：这个构件的作用怎样真正交给下一个构件，而不能因为两个部件在图上或空间上靠得很近，就假定力可以跨过空隙。
本模型只追踪新增托座形成的一条支路，并不假设三枚硬币的全部重量都只经过这一根柱。没有托座时，模型仍通过其他接触、支承和变形重新分配作用；装上托座后，只是多了一条实际连续的向下传递路线。

moduleZh.intro: 固定硬币位置、模型主体和其他支承，只拆装一个托座，观察附近的粗柱何时真正加入向下传力路线。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 粗柱一直都在，为什么只有加上托座后它才真正参与传力
diagramSteps: 三枚硬币按固定叠法放在角落黄色圆点上，平台角下沉
检查底面：横梁端部没有落到旁边的粗柱上
先移开挡位说明牌，再装托座；面板、梁、柱、底座和其他支承不换
同样硬币、位置和叠法下，装上托座平台保持，拆掉后下沉复现
取走硬币，重新装回托座，保留移开的说明牌，再用于展示
diagramStepNotes: 固定数量、位置和叠法，避免把荷载摆法变化当成托座效果。
梁和柱靠得近不等于已接通；没有托座时，重量仍经其余接触、支承和变形重新分配。
说明牌先腾位置，托座才真正承在梁端和柱顶之间；这只是桌面模型构造。
拆装支承前先取走硬币，再复放比较；新增托座只是一条支路，不独自承担全部重量。
承压接触与抗上拔连接不同。保留展示空间代价，不把本模型当成真实结构验收。
mapping: 三枚硬币 → 固定位置上的教学重力荷载。
未接上的粗柱 → 附近很强但尚未进入该传力路线的构件。
小托座 → 让横梁向下作用真实进入立柱的承压支承。
移开的透明说明牌 → 为连续实际支承让出空间所付出的展示代价。
moduleZh.boundary: 这是只处理向下重力的桌面模型，不提供真实建筑承载、抗风抗震、改造或安全验收依据。承压接触能在压缩方向传力，并不自动意味着在上拔、侧向或反向作用下仍具有所需连接能力。真实结构还需检查各构件、连接和基础在具体方向上的能力以及完整连续路径。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果作用方向改成向上拉，这只靠承压接触放置的托座能自动沿用吗？应怎样检查各环节在新方向上是否真的能传力？

referencesZh.citation: Federal Emergency Management Agency. (2010, December). Wind Retrofit Guide for Residential Buildings. FEMA P-804, sections 3.1.2 and 4.3.1, pp. 3-4–3-5 and 4-21–4-23.
referencesZh.use: 支持连续荷载路径需要通过真实结构构件和连接把作用传至基础与地面，以及缺失连接会中断预期传力；也支持连接能力与受力方向有关。本篇只借用该连接原则解释低风险桌面重力模型，不作为真实建筑规范合规或改造依据。

articles.title: The Gap Beside the Thick Column
articles.summary: Three coins make one corner of the platform model drop. Gu Yan looks at the thick column beside it and wonders why it has done nothing to help.
storyParagraphs: A community building exhibition is preparing a palm-sized platform model. Visitors will be able to stack three coins on a yellow dot at one corner and watch how the model carries the weight downward. When Gu Yan rehearses the demonstration, the platform corner drops and the three coins slide down the tilted surface onto the table. The strange part is that a small column thicker than the others is standing right beside the spot that moves.

Gu Yan lifts the model and looks underneath. The beam supports the deck, but its end passes beside the thick column’s top instead of actually bearing on it. The two parts are close, yet a gap remains. He leaves the column in place and looks for a small bracket that will fit between them.

A transparent information card blocks the space between the beam end and the column top. Gu Yan moves it outside the model before fitting the small bracket. He keeps the original deck, beam, column, base and other supports. He returns the same three coins to the yellow dot in the same arrangement, and this time the platform stays up. He traces the new branch: deck to beam, through the bracket to the column, then part of the weight through the base to the table.

Gu Yan removes the coins, takes out the bracket, then returns the three coins in the same position and arrangement. The corner drops again. He removes the coins once more and reinstalls the bracket. The relocated information card makes the display look more cluttered, but he leaves it outside the model so the bracket remains fully visible.

Once the exhibition opens, a visitor picks up the three demonstration coins and stacks them again on the yellow dot. The platform no longer tilts down. She bends to look underneath, sees the bracket exposed below the beam, points first to it and then to the base, and asks, “So only after this is really connected is there a route downward?” Gu Yan turns the model slightly toward her. “Yes. This branch is connected now.” The three coins remain on the yellow dot.
articles.overall: This article uses a low-risk tabletop gravity model to introduce one aspect of a load path: a load must pass continuously through actual structural members and direction-appropriate contacts or connections to supports and ultimately to the foundation or ground. The mere presence of a strong member nearby is not enough; if a real transfer step is missing, that member does not automatically join the load path being considered.
explanationParagraphs: A downward gravity load can pass through a deck, beam, actual bearing support, column, and base in sequence. To trace the path, ask at every step how one member actually transfers its action to the next; two components being close together in a drawing or in space does not allow force to jump across a gap.

This model follows only the additional branch created by the new bracket and does not assume that all the weight of the three coins passes exclusively through this one column. Without the bracket, the model still redistributes action through its other contacts, supports, and deformation. Adding the bracket simply creates another physically continuous downward transfer route.

module.intro: Keep the coin location, main model components, and other supports fixed, change only whether one bracket is present, and observe when the nearby thick column actually joins the downward load-transfer route.
module.diagramTitle: The Thick Column Was Always There—Why Does It Participate Only After the Bracket Is Added?
diagramSteps: Stack three coins in the fixed arrangement on the yellow corner dot; the corner drops
Inspect underneath: the beam end does not bear on the nearby thick column
Move the obstructing card before fitting the bracket; keep the deck, beam, column, base and other supports
With the same coins, location and arrangement, the platform stays up with the bracket and drops again without it
Remove the coins, reinstall the bracket, leave the card relocated and return the model to the exhibition
diagramStepNotes: Fix quantity, position and stacking arrangement so a changed load placement is not mistaken for a bracket effect.
Closeness is not a connection. Without the bracket, weight is still redistributed through other contacts, supports and deformation.
Clear the card first so the bracket can actually bear between beam end and column top. This is only a tabletop-model detail.
Remove coins before changing support, then replace them for comparison. The new bracket is one branch, not the sole carrier of all weight.
Bearing contact differs from an uplift connection. Keep the display-space trade-off without treating the model as real structural approval.
mapping: Three coins → the teaching gravity load at a fixed position.
Thick but unconnected column → a nearby strong member that has not yet entered the intended load-transfer route.
Small bracket → the bearing support that allows downward action from the beam to enter the column.
Relocated transparent information card → the display-space cost of making room for a real continuous support.
module.boundary: This is a tabletop model dealing only with downward gravity. It provides no basis for real-building capacity, wind or earthquake design, retrofit work, or safety approval. Bearing contact can transfer compression in the direction for which it is engaged, but it does not automatically provide the connection required for uplift, lateral action, or reversed loading. Real structures require checking the capacity of every member, connection, and foundation in the relevant direction and verifying the complete continuous load path.
module.reflection: If the applied load pulls upward instead, can this bracket, engaged only through bearing contact, automatically be used in the same way? What must be checked at each transfer step in the new direction?

references.citation: Federal Emergency Management Agency. (2010, December). Wind Retrofit Guide for Residential Buildings. FEMA P-804, sections 3.1.2 and 4.3.1, pp. 3-4–3-5 and 4-21–4-23.
references.use: Supports the principle that a continuous load path transfers applied loads through actual structural members and connections to foundations and ground, that missing connections interrupt intended load transfer, and that connection requirements depend on load direction. This article uses that connection principle only for a low-risk tabletop gravity model and not as a claim of real-building code compliance or retrofit adequacy.

articles.summaryZh: 展陈团队准备把一套支臂方案交给制作方。主体计算已告一段落，林澈点开发送窗口时，却发现还有一处连接需要再看一眼。
storyParagraphsZh: 展陈团队下午要把一套不载人的展示支臂方案发给制作方，决定下一轮样机长什么样。细支臂已经改了几轮，屏幕上的这一版最利落，负责外观的同事正等林澈点发送。支臂本体那页也不再让人皱眉：在这套纸面荷载案例中，所选屈服判据的预测极限力是120牛顿（N），对应工作需求是60 N。
前几轮大家一直围着这根支臂加厚、改形。120除以60得到2，会议气氛松了下来。外观同事准备收起样机盒，林澈点开发送窗口，又扫了一眼剩下的接口计算。
鼠标停在底部夹具那一行。这里问的不是支臂会不会达到所选屈服判据，而是连接会不会先发生滑移。工程师对同一荷载案例，按夹具尚未滑移的假定构型估算，滑移方向的工作需求碰巧也是60 N，预测滑移极限却只有45 N。林澈按了计算器：45÷60=0.75。支臂那一项的2仍然成立，却不能替夹具回答这一项。
她把发送窗口关掉。团队原本还在讨论要不要继续给支臂加材料，现在决定先保持支臂不动，把底部连接交回接口设计去修改，再用修订后的方案重新检查各自对应的判据。这样会推迟下一轮样机制作，原本藏得很干净的接口也可能需要更多空间，但继续强化已经有余量的支臂，并不能解决眼前暴露出来的连接问题。
散会前，林澈把细支臂留在样机上，只卸下底部夹具交给负责接口的人。外观同事把刚准备收走的样机盒又放回桌边：“那这一版先不发？”林澈点头：“等接口回来，再一起看。”制作文件仍停在草稿状态。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用虚构纸面设计比较说明安全系数的一个入口：对明确对象、工况、方向和失效模式，可以把预测极限抗力与相应工作需求这两个同类物理量相除，得到无量纲比值。这个比值只回答所定义的那一项裕度，不能自动覆盖另一种失效模式，也不是事故概率、普适安全门槛或整套构造的安全证明。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本篇采用一种“计算得到的比值”用法：安全系数=某一明确失效模式下的预测极限抗力÷同一工况下、同一对象口径和相同物理量的工作需求。分子和分母必须能够直接比较；不同方向、不同判据或不同物理量不能随意相除。
最小例子：支臂屈服判据下预测极限力120 N、对应工作需求60 N，则120/60=2。另对同一荷载案例，按夹具滑移前的假定构型估算滑移方向需求为60 N，预测滑移极限45 N，则45/60=0.75：纸面需求高于这一预测极限。这提示该模式需重新核查，不代表实物已按纸面数值验证失效；一旦发生滑移，受力也可能重新分配。

moduleZh.intro: 先把一个比值绑定到明确对象和失效模式，再检查系统中是否还有另一个比值正在回答不同的问题。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么支臂的比值是2，仍不能替夹具的滑移判据作结论
diagramSteps: 在固定展示工况和方向下，计算支臂屈服判据对应的工作需求60 N
用该判据的预测极限力120 N除以60 N，得到无量纲比值2
继续检查底部夹具滑移判据：同一荷载案例下，按滑移前假定构型估算其滑移方向需求为60 N
用预测滑移极限45 N除以该需求60 N，得到0.75
暂缓这一版制作，先修改连接，再重新核查相关失效模式
diagramStepNotes: 第一个60 N只属于支臂屈服判据在该工况下的匹配需求，不是所有构件天然都承受同一力。
120 N是虚构纸面预测极限值，不是实测额定值；屈服判据也不等同于必然断裂。
第二个60 N是针对夹具滑移方向、按滑移前构型另行估算的需求；相同数值只是本教学例设定，不是实测“未滑移”状态。
0.75暴露的是这一局部滑移判据需要重新检查，不能据此断言真实装置已经发生失效。
不同失效模式需要分别检查，一个局部高比值不能覆盖稳定、连接、疲劳、材料或整体其他模式。
mapping: 120 N与60 N → 支臂屈服判据下可比较的预测极限力与工作需求。
45 N与60 N → 夹具滑移判据下另一组可比较的预测极限力与工作需求。
关闭发送窗口 → 一个局部指标不足以支持整套方案继续深化后的实际选择变化。
拆下夹具 → 把下一步工作转到当前暴露出的连接模式。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只演示一种“预测极限抗力÷相应工作需求”的计算比值。工程文献中“factor of safety”也可能指设计方法中预先规定的乘数，不能与本例计算比值混为一谈；许用应力设计中的允许值也不能直接当作实际工作应力。现代规范还可能使用分项荷载和抗力系数。所有120 N、60 N、45 N均为虚构纸面教学值，不是建筑设计参数、规范要求、施工指引或普适门槛。
moduleZh.reflection: 另一个构件在指定屈服判据下，预测极限为80 N、对应需求为50 N，比值是多少？它能直接说明该构件连接的滑移判据也有足够裕度吗？

referencesZh.citation: Ramsey, J. K. (2019, September). Calculating Factors of Safety and Margins of Safety From Interaction Equations. NASA/TM—2019-220153, Appendix A. NASA Glenn Research Center.
referencesZh.use: 支持安全系数术语可指相同物理量之间计算得到的比值，也可在其他语境中指预先规定的乘数，具体定义取决于方法与上下文；本篇只采用前一种教学用法，不把NASA方法当作建筑规范或通用数值要求。

referencesZh.citation: Hooks, J., & Frangopol, D. M. (2013, December). LTBP Bridge Performance Primer. FHWA-HRT-13-051. Federal Highway Administration.
referencesZh.use: 支持理解许用应力设计中的安全系数概念以及现代LRFD使用不同荷载与抗力分项系数的区别；该技术资料不是标准、规范或法规，本篇不把其中的许用应力概念等同于实际工作应力或现实设计值。

articles.title: The Drawing That Stayed Unsent
articles.summary: An exhibition team is ready to send its display-arm design to the fabricator. The main arm calculation looks reassuring, but as Lin Che opens the send window, one connection still needs a closer look.
storyParagraphs: That afternoon, the exhibition team is about to send a display-arm design not intended to support people to the fabricator and decide what the next prototype will look like. The slender arm has gone through several revisions, and the version on screen is the cleanest yet. The colleague responsible for appearance waits for Lin Che to click Send. The arm calculation page is reassuring too: in this paper load case, the selected yield criterion has a predicted limiting force of 120 newtons (N) and a corresponding demand of 60 N.

For the past several rounds, everyone has been thickening and reshaping the arm. Dividing 120 by 60 gives 2, and the mood in the meeting relaxes. The appearance colleague starts to pack away the prototype box. Lin Che opens the send window and gives the remaining interface calculations one last look.

Her cursor stops on the base-clamp line. The question is no longer whether the arm reaches the selected yield criterion, but whether the connection might slip first. For the same load case, engineers estimate the demand in the slip direction using an assumed configuration before the clamp slips. It happens to be 60 N, while the predicted slip limit is only 45 N. Lin Che taps the calculator: 45÷60=0.75. The arm’s ratio of 2 still stands, but it cannot answer the clamp’s question.

She closes the send window. The team had still been discussing whether to add more material to the arm, but now they decide to leave the arm unchanged, send the base connection back for revision, and then recheck the corresponding criteria using the revised scheme. This will delay the next prototype, and an interface that had been neatly hidden may need more space, but adding more material to an arm that already has margin does not solve the connection issue that has now appeared.

Before the meeting ends, Lin Che leaves the slender arm on the prototype and removes only the base clamp, handing it to the person responsible for the interface. The appearance colleague puts the prototype box, which had just been about to be packed away, back beside the table. “So this version doesn't go out yet?” Lin Che nods. “Wait until the interface comes back, then we'll look at it together.” The fabrication file remains in draft.
articles.overall: This article uses a fictional paper design comparison to introduce one meaning of factor of safety: for a clearly defined object, operating condition, direction, and failure mode, a dimensionless ratio can be calculated by dividing predicted limiting resistance by the corresponding working demand when the numerator and denominator are directly comparable physical quantities. That ratio answers only the margin defined for that case. It does not automatically cover another failure mode, and it is not an accident probability, a universal safety threshold, or proof that an entire assembly is safe.
explanationParagraphs: This article uses the calculated-ratio meaning: factor of safety = predicted limiting resistance for a clearly defined failure mode ÷ the corresponding working demand for the same operating condition, object definition, and physical quantity. The numerator and denominator must be directly comparable; quantities from different directions, criteria, or physical measures cannot simply be divided.

Minimal example: for the arm yield criterion, a predicted limiting force of 120 N and corresponding demand of 60 N give 120/60=2. For the same load case, estimate the clamp’s demand in the slip direction using an assumed pre-slip configuration: 60 N against a predicted slip limit of 45 N gives 45/60=0.75. The paper demand exceeds that predicted limit, so this mode needs rechecking. It does not establish that a real prototype has failed as the figures suggest; if slip occurs, forces may redistribute.

module.intro: First bind each ratio to a specific object and failure mode, then check whether another part of the system has a different ratio answering a different question.
module.diagramTitle: Why a Ratio of 2 for the Arm Cannot Answer the Clamp's Slip Criterion
diagramSteps: Under a fixed display operating condition and direction, calculate a 60 N working demand corresponding to the arm yield criterion
Divide the predicted limiting force of 120 N for that criterion by 60 N to obtain the dimensionless ratio 2
For the same load case, estimate the clamp’s demand in the slip direction as 60 N using an assumed pre-slip configuration
Divide the predicted slip limit of 45 N by that 60 N demand to obtain 0.75
Pause fabrication of this version, revise the connection first, and then recheck the relevant failure modes
diagramStepNotes: The first 60 N belongs specifically to the arm yield criterion under this operating condition; it does not mean every component naturally carries the same force.
The 120 N value is a fictional predicted paper limit, not a tested rated value, and a yield criterion is not the same as inevitable fracture.
The second 60 N is separately estimated in the clamp’s slip direction using a pre-slip configuration. Its equal value is a teaching assumption, not an observed no-slip state.
The 0.75 result identifies a local slip criterion that requires further checking; it does not prove that the real device has already failed.
Different failure modes require separate checks. A high local ratio cannot cover stability, connections, fatigue, material behavior, or other system-level modes.
mapping: 120 N and 60 N → the predicted limiting force and working demand that are directly comparable for the arm yield criterion.
45 N and 60 N → a separate pair of directly comparable predicted limiting force and working demand for the clamp slip criterion.
Closing the send window → the practical decision change after one local metric proves insufficient to support the whole scheme.
Removing the clamp → shifting the next design effort toward the currently exposed connection mode.
module.boundary: This article demonstrates only one calculated form of factor of safety: predicted limiting resistance divided by corresponding working demand. In engineering literature, “factor of safety” can also refer in other contexts to a prescribed multiplier used within a design method; that use must not be confused with the calculated ratio shown here. Allowable values in allowable-stress design also must not be treated as actual working stress. Modern codes may instead use separate load and resistance factors. All values of 120 N, 60 N, and 45 N are fictional teaching values, not building-design parameters, code requirements, construction guidance, or universal thresholds.
module.reflection: For another component, a specified yield criterion has a predicted limit of 80 N and a corresponding demand of 50 N. What is the ratio? Does it establish that the connection also has sufficient margin against slip?

references.citation: Ramsey, J. K. (2019, September). Calculating Factors of Safety and Margins of Safety From Interaction Equations. NASA/TM—2019-220153, Appendix A. NASA Glenn Research Center.
references.use: Supports that factor-of-safety terminology can refer to a calculated ratio between like physical quantities and, in other contexts, to a prescribed multiplying factor, with the definition depending on the method and context. This article uses only the former teaching meaning and does not treat NASA methods as building codes or universal numerical requirements.

references.citation: Hooks, J., & Frangopol, D. M. (2013, December). LTBP Bridge Performance Primer. FHWA-HRT-13-051. Federal Highway Administration.
references.use: Supports the conceptual distinction between factor of safety in allowable-stress design and the use of separate load and resistance factors in modern LRFD approaches. This technical primer is not a standard, specification, or regulation, and the article does not treat allowable stress as actual working stress or use the source as a basis for real design values.

articles.summaryZh: 林澈今天要提交公共通道更新方案。较贵的方案会挤压今年的照明预算，维护负责人却让她再看一张表。
storyParagraphsZh: 社区中心旁的公共步行通道准备更新，林澈要在当天把方案送进预算会。A方案今年需要30个计价单位，B方案需要42；如果选B，多出的12个单位就得从今年另一项入口照明更新里腾出来。她已经把A放到推荐栏里，因为眼前的预算缺口是真实存在的。
维护负责人来找她时，没有要求她把A划掉，只问了一句：“这条通道六年里谁来养？”他把两套维护安排放到桌上：A以后每年需要5个计价单位的维护支出，B每年需要2个。林澈原本只留了一栏给建设费用，现在不得不把表格往右拉长。
她把六个年份依次写进去。A后面连续出现六个“5”，B后面是六个“2”。最开始那两个醒目的数字30和42都没有消失；只是A今年少付12个单位的优势旁边，第一次出现了未来几年反复承担的支出。林澈把手从“提交”键上移开，重新打开了今年和后续年度的预算说明。
这并没有让选择突然变得轻松。B会让今年的入口照明更新推迟，A则把更多已设定的维护支出留到以后。林澈没有把任何一边直接圈成赢家，而是让两套方案都按同样的六年服务任务进入会议材料，并把今年要让出的照明项目单独列在旁边。
预算会开始前，她把新表放到每个座位上。第一页仍然能看见30和42，后面多了六列。负责今年预算的人先指向那12个单位，维护负责人则指向后面的年份。林澈翻开旁边的照明项目说明，等两人看完，再把通道的维护安排摊在中间。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一项六年公共通道服务比较说明基础设施全生命周期管理的一个入口：决策不能只停在初始建设价格，还要把同一服务和时间范围内的运行维护、更新等后续责任一起考虑。全生命周期视角的目标是持续提供服务，而不是简单寻找开场最便宜或维护支出最低的方案。
articles.conceptNameZh: 基础设施全生命周期管理
explanationParagraphsZh: 为把数字放在同一口径下，本教学算例明确假设A、B提供相同的六年服务，六年末均无残值，所有费用使用同一实价口径，贴现率假设为0，并排除其他服务差异。在这些条件下，A的六年支出为30+5×6=60个计价单位；B为42+2×6=54个计价单位。因此本例中B虽然初建多12个单位，按这组设定计算的六年总支出却少6个单位。
这个结果只是一个决策入口，不表示更贵的初装方案通常更便宜，也不表示维护支出越低、越早或越多就一定更好。真实基础设施管理还要结合资产状态、服务水平、风险、不确定性、资金时点、长期需求、残值和适当的时间价值处理；未经核实的远期费用也不能与当期支出随意相加。这60与54只计算通道本身的设定支出，没有把照明更新延期造成的收益变化或其他后果计价，不能替两个项目作整体排序。

moduleZh.intro: 先固定相同的服务任务和时间范围，再把初始建设与后续维护支出放到同一口径比较，同时保留当期资金约束。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么A今年少付12个单位，仍不足以回答哪套六年方案支出更低
diagramSteps: 把A和B放在相同的六年公共通道服务范围内比较
记录初建支出：A为30个计价单位，B为42个
记录六年维护支出：A每年5个单位，B每年2个

articles.title: Six More Columns in the Budget
articles.summary: Lin Che must submit a walkway upgrade plan today. The dearer option would squeeze this year’s lighting budget, but the maintenance manager asks her to look at another table.
storyParagraphs: The public walkway beside the community centre is due for an upgrade, and Lin Che has to submit a plan to the budget meeting that day. Option A requires 30 accounting units this year, while option B requires 42. If they choose B, the extra 12 units will have to come out of another entrance-lighting upgrade scheduled for this year. She has already placed A in the recommendation column because the immediate budget gap is real.

When the maintenance manager comes to see her, he does not ask her to cross out A. He asks only one question: “Who is going to look after this walkway over the next six years?” He places two maintenance schedules on the table: A requires 5 accounting units of maintenance expenditure each year, while B requires 2 each year. Lin Che had originally left only one column for construction cost; now she has to extend the table to the right.

She writes in the six years one by one. Six consecutive 5s appear after A, and six 2s after B. The two prominent opening figures, 30 and 42, have not disappeared. But beside A's 12-unit advantage this year, the expenditure that will recur in later years appears for the first time. Lin Che moves her hand away from the “submit” button and reopens the budget notes for this year and the following years.

That does not suddenly make the choice easy. B would delay this year's entrance-lighting upgrade, while A would leave more of the specified maintenance expenditure for later years. Lin Che does not circle either side as the winner. Instead, she puts both options into the meeting papers under the same six-year service task and lists the lighting project that would have to give way this year separately beside them.

Before the budget meeting begins, she places the new table at every seat. The first page still shows 30 and 42, followed by six more columns. The person responsible for this year’s budget points first to the 12 units; the maintenance manager points to the later years. Lin Che opens the lighting project notes beside them. When both have finished reading, she lays the walkway maintenance schedules between them.
articles.overall: This article uses a six-year public-walkway service comparison to introduce one aspect of infrastructure life-cycle management: a decision should not stop at the initial construction price but should also consider subsequent responsibilities such as operation, maintenance, and renewal over the same service scope and time period. A life-cycle perspective aims to sustain service rather than simply identify the cheapest opening price or the lowest maintenance expenditure.
explanationParagraphs: To place the figures on a common basis, this teaching example explicitly assumes that A and B provide the same six-year service, both have zero residual value at the end of year six, all costs are expressed on the same real-price basis, the discount rate is assumed to be 0, and other service differences are excluded. Under those conditions, A's six-year expenditure is 30+5×6=60 accounting units, while B's is 42+2×6=54. In this example, B therefore costs 12 units more initially but 6 units less over the six years under the stated assumptions.

This result is only an entry point for decision-making. It does not mean that more expensive initial installation is generally cheaper over the life cycle, nor that lower, earlier, or greater maintenance expenditure is always better. Real infrastructure management also has to consider asset condition, service level, risk, uncertainty, timing of funds, long-term demand, residual value, and appropriate treatment of the time value of money. Unverified future costs also cannot simply be added to current expenditure without a sound common basis. The totals of 60 and 54 cover only the specified walkway expenditure. They do not price the benefits or other consequences of postponing the lighting upgrade and cannot rank the two projects as a whole.

module.intro: First fix the same service task and time period, then compare initial construction and later maintenance expenditure on the same basis while keeping current funding constraints visible.
module.diagramTitle: Why Is A's 12-Unit Saving This Year Still Not Enough to Answer Which Six-Year Option Costs Less?
diagramSteps: Compare A and B over the same six-year public-walkway service scope
Record initial expenditure: A is 30 accounting units and B is 42
Record six years of maintenance expenditure: A is 5 units per year and B is 2
Under the teaching assumptions of zero residual value, the same real-price basis, and a 0 discount rate, calculate A as 60 and B as 54
Bring the six-year comparison into the decision together with the fact that B uses an extra 12 units this year and delays the lighting upgrade
diagramStepNotes: If the service scope or comparison period differs, comparing totals no longer has a common basis.
42 is 12 units more than 30, and that current funding difference does not disappear simply because a life-cycle perspective is used.
The comparison here concerns annual maintenance expenditure amounts, not maintenance frequency, and it does not infer which option experiences fewer failures.
The totals of 60 and 54 hold only under the explicitly stated six-year, zero-residual-value, same-real-price, 0-discount-rate assumptions with other differences excluded.
Life-cycle management has to consider both long-term service responsibilities and the timing of funds rather than allowing a long-term total automatically to override this year's budget constraint.
mapping: A initial cost 30 → the lower current construction expenditure.
B initial cost 42 → construction expenditure that uses 12 more units this year and squeezes another project.
A maintenance 5 per year and B maintenance 2 per year → the specified continuing maintenance expenditure over the six-year service period.
A total 60 and B total 54 → the six-year expenditure comparison under the unified teaching assumptions.
Delayed entrance-lighting upgrade → the concrete current-budget trade-off created by the long-term option choice.
module.boundary: The figures 30, 42, 5, 2, 60, and 54 in this example are fictional teaching values, not real engineering quotations. Infrastructure life-cycle management does not mean always choosing the option with the higher initial cost or the lower annual maintenance expenditure, and it does not mean that maintenance is always better when it happens earlier or more often. Real decisions need to consider asset condition, risk, service demand, uncertainty, funding constraints, residual value, and appropriate discounting. This story provides no real infrastructure design, maintenance interval, failure probability, or procurement conclusion.
module.reflection: If the options need to provide only three years of service instead of six, which costs and end-of-period values would you check again? Why can you not simply reuse the totals of 60 and 54?
